reviews.author: Cory H.
reviews.text: We camped at Fairholme 17 years ago and enjoyed it then, but being back this year for the 4th of July was even better than the first time. The camp ground is immaculate. One of the best camp hosts I’ve ever met was working there all week, he was amazing. Even though we were camped in loop C without direct like lake access, we went down on the morning of the fourth and spent an amazing morning, paddle boarding and reading enjoying the water. Only downside is that we couldn’t find any showers even though the website listed them. All in all an amazing campground. Highly recommended!

reviews.author: Simin W.
reviews.text: Overall is good. The campsites are a bit compact.

reviews.author: Mo L.
reviews.text: I would highly recommend swimming, whether it is morning, day, or night. Enjoy the moss and the cars driving by on route 101 at 80mph in the middle of the night!

reviews.author: Rob H.
reviews.text: The overall campground area is nice. We were at A4, there was no privacy from other campgrounds surrounding us and we could see the men's bathroom entrance from our campsite. The trails and paths around the area are well kept just wish for more privacy.

reviews.author: Carolina B.
reviews.text: We stayed here for two nights, both of which were perfect. Everything was clean, from the bathrooms to the campsite. Being right on the lake was beautiful. While we did venture out to other parts of the park for some hiking, you could certainly spend multiple days at Fairholme and not get bored just sticking around! We will hopefully be back soon.

reviews.author: Kathryn B.
reviews.text: What a beautiful campground in Olympic N.P.! I walked down to Lake Crescent in the morning and it's really breathtaking. Our site was clean and even though it was steps from the road that continued on the north side of the lake- only 1 car ever went down the road in our time camped there. I highly recommend this CG! Quiet and beautiful.

reviews.author: Merelin C.
reviews.text:
The best thing about this campsite is the lake. Unfortunately, I never really felt “unplugged.” The road noise was constant throughout our stay, with lots of large trucks driving by that felt disruptive to the natural setting. At one point, I found a quiet moment where I could hear the leaves rustling, but it was immediately drowned out by traffic.

The campsites are also very close together, so there’s essentially no privacy. I found myself constantly—and unintentionally—making eye contact with neighboring campers and people walking through the campground.

We stayed at Site 87, and while we had a nice waterfront spot, it did require a bit of a walk to reach the water. The tent pad was also quite uneven, which made setting up more challenging. The site itself felt small. It was fine for my husband, our toddler, and me, but it’s listed for up to eight people, and I honestly can’t imagine fitting more than one tent there comfortably.

The bathrooms were very clean, which I appreciated.

Overall, when I think of camping, I want to feel immersed in nature and disconnected from the outside world. This was a nice place to spend time with family and friends, away from home, but the constant road noise didn’t allow me the take in nature as much as I wanted to. 

There were squirrels that were a bit too comfortable with being close to us. The food lockers were helpful for this situation. 

That said, I would camp here again if I were planning to spend my days paddling on the lake, but not if I were looking to relax and unwind after a long hike.

reviews.author: Mollie K.
reviews.text: Loved this place. Had driven on the way to Forks a few times and always wanted to stop. We really enjoyed it!!!

reviews.author: Wen H.
reviews.text: This specific site is not flat and slightly sloped. Just be aware when setting up a tent at this site. This specific campsite does have more privacy than other nearby sites, which was nice. Lake Crescent is easily accessible from the campground. Bathrooms have flushing toilets. The general store is adjacent to the campground. You do hear some road noise but our family did not find it bothersome. Our family used this campsite as a base to explore most of Olympic NP.

reviews.author: nurit y.
reviews.text: Great location and view by the lake . Rv dump station

reviews.author: Tamara S.
reviews.text: The sites I had along the lake were absolutely amazing. The walk in experience allowed for that. The hosts were incredibly helpful and friendly and were doing excellent at keeping everything running smoothly.

reviews.author: Yongmiao W.
reviews.text: No showers and no hand soap provided, but the lake view is breathtaking.

reviews.author: John H.
reviews.text: Need more bear boxes.  And trash needs to be emptied more often.  It was overr

reviews.author: Gregory  M.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground on a beautiful lake. Campsites were great and the campground was super quiet in the mornings. We loved everything about it!

reviews.author: Christian Y.
reviews.text: Beautiful and quiet campground. The lake is viewable at least partially from most campsites. Our site had perfect tree coverage. Site was spacious. Highly recommend this specific site and this campground

reviews.author: Sydney m.
reviews.text:
Such a great campground! Campsite was clean and comfortable. It’s not very private but my family and I didn’t mind. Very family friendly. My only complaint is there are very few toilets available and they get VERY busy. Often had to wait in line. They also weren’t cleaned often so 1 of 2 women’s toilets were clogged and out of TP almost my entire stay.
Definitely booking this campground again :)

reviews.author: Kristin H.
reviews.text: We enjoyed a quiet night here. If you want a fire, be sure to get your firewood when you see it available. Both places we looked for nearby were sold out by 5pm. The tent area was nice and flat.

reviews.author: Kayla N.
reviews.text: Beautiful spot, but I did fall down the steep gravel slope you go down to get to the spot. Also, not a good spot if it takes multiple trips to the car to get your supplies. If you camp super light, then this is a good spot unless you don't mind going up and down the hill from the parking lot. Just be careful going down that slope.

reviews.author: Robyn E.
reviews.text: Quiet sites, beautiful lake, lots of hikes nearby. The “walk to” for this specific campsite is very short, in case you are worried about it, and the bathrooms are also very close.

reviews.author: Camryn D.
reviews.text: In the area where we stayed, the sites were very close together without many trees to provide privacy. We arrived in mid-June and did not prepare well for the onslaught of flies. We'd like to give this place another try, because Crescent Lake was incredibly beautiful and just a short walk from the campsites.

reviews.author: Amina H.
reviews.text: beautiful lake, clean bathrooms, but no soap dispensers

reviews.author: Adoracion  A.
reviews.text:
Site is spacious. Very private. The afternoon sun does hit the area but the sun feels good and gives you an opportunity to dry your clothes after swimming in the lake. 

We also booked site 3 and it was not a private site. Site 2 and 23 is practically is right next to it. It’s great if you can book the other 2 sites so it can seem like a group site. It’s right across the bathroom and water which is convenient if you have kids but it’s also next to the path for people to get to the bathroom. Overall good site but loop A offers little to no privacy. loop C is more private.

reviews.author: Nadiia  V.
reviews.text:
My family visited this campground for the first time, and since we wanted to try it out, we booked just one night. We loved it and will definitely come back for a longer stay next year.

The nature is incredible, everything is clean, and it’s obvious that the campground is well maintained. The restrooms are in good condition and even have electrical outlets. The campsites are laid out very well, with plenty of space and protection from the blazing sun. Even on a hot day, we felt comfortable.

There is a lake nearby and a store within easy reach. Throughout the day, rangers drove through several times to make sure everything was in order.

In short, I highly recommend this place. It’s a fantastic campground!

reviews.author: richard w.
reviews.text:
The system worked very well for us.  We were fortunate to book campsites at all the places we were hoping.

Thank you!
Rick

reviews.author: kathy r.
reviews.text: What a great park!  It was a very quiet park and yet a lot of people.  The campsites were nicely spaced.  The restrooms were somewhat clean but yet the campground was full so that needs to be taken into account.  Hiking trails were very accessible and so was biking.  Crescent Lake is beautiful and water sports is highly recommended.  I'd go back again.

reviews.author: Svitlana  B.
reviews.text: Great and clean place!

reviews.author: Kristin B.
reviews.text: Clean and room between spaces. Beautiful scenery and easy drive to popular parts of this very large park!

reviews.author: Chris B.
reviews.text: The noise from the highway was loud and constant, which ruined an otherwise beautiful campground. Even in the middle of the night you can hear big trucks, logging trucks, and cars rumbling through Highway 101. Could not sleep at all.

reviews.author: John C.
reviews.text: Quite possible the most beautiful campsite we’ve ever stayed in. Ridiculously tall, huge trees, moss everywhere , simply stunning

reviews.author: Jesse M.
reviews.text: One of the most beautiful places on earth.

reviews.author: Emma M.
reviews.text: Loved this campground and our site! I was worried based on other reviews about the slant, but there was a flat area perfect for our tent and the table was easy to level out by putting sticks under the legs. It had a perfect hammock set up right by the water!

reviews.author: Denise L.
reviews.text: What an unexpected treat.  This campground is a wonderful central location for the north end of the peninsula.  There is a wonderful trail that extends all the way to Devil's Punchbowl (usually accessed from the east side road).  There are other campground loop trails that take you through magnificent trees.  And then there's the fabulous lake.  It's just a spectacular place.  The parking areas of the campsites are not very even, but other than that, it's a gem!  And there's a store in case you need anything.  Perfect!

reviews.author: Stewart S.
reviews.text: Our first trip back in ten years! I have been going there since the late seventies, a lot of great memories with my children, miss the programs at the amphitheater, Smoky the Bear and a Ranger coming around and inviting everyone to the program, and of course the fellow with the boys and old truck driving each loop saying over a loud speaker “ Firewood, Firewood for sale “ Definitely good times gone by now! But still had a blast!

reviews.author: Debbie K.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground with lots of lush trees and shade. Parking at our site was adequate. We have one really large tent that easily sat on a mostly flat portion of the site. There is an easy (mild elevation but short loop) walking trail accessible from the campground. Bathrooms were easily accessed from many sites. Bathrooms were mostly clean but I will complain that there was no soap and no hooks, hangers or shelf space to keep your toilet kit. A bulletin board is just outside the bathrooms with some useful info. I wish it also had nearby trail info with access points and distances. I did not have occasion to encounter the camp host.

reviews.author: Jackie  M.
reviews.text:
The bathroom was modern and clean, but they don’t appear to want you to use soap, as there was no soap dispenser. We tried putting out some soap, but it disappeared almost immediately, I think the cleaning crew took it. Not sure why soap is taboo.

Many of the spaces in A loop are small, and not very private. We had a hard time finding a place to put a small 3 person tent and a tiny 1 person tent. Many of the campsites were a bit nicer, but very few have ample space for more than a single tent. Although the campground was supposed to be full, quite a few people seemed to show up, not like their site, and ask the camp host if they could move. This happened a lot on the end by the bathroom.

Nice, central location for exploring the peninsula, and good lake access.

reviews.author: Megan P.
reviews.text: This campground is so beautiful, well spread out and bathrooms are clean

reviews.author: Steve W.
reviews.text: Amazing park.  Quiet.  Very attentive camp hosts.  Clean facilities.  Definitely will be back

reviews.author: Ashlynn D.
reviews.text: super sick walk in spots right on the lake! very quiet and so stunning

reviews.author: Pearl J.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground. Lovely views of the lake and surrounding mountains!

reviews.author: carolyn a.
reviews.text: Don’t let your dogs chase the ducks respectfully

reviews.author: John W.
reviews.text:
The campsite was nice and in a good location. My site was overlooking the water down the hill, but with trees in between. We were able to walk down to the water easily and paddle board from there.

The site itself was a little small, but still big enough for all of our equipment so no complaints. There was also a picnic table and firepit at the site. And a parking space that was big enough for 2 or 3 cars. The campground also has flush toilets which is always nice.

There is a general store next to the campground that sells pretty much anything you could need, including firewood, ice, snacks, and icecream.

We had been to Olympic National Park before so didn't venture off too much. We visited the Lake Crescent Lodge and sat by the water for a bit. There are also many trails nearby.

reviews.author: Joachim S.
reviews.text:
Amazing camping ground. Clean, absolutely beautiful, spacious...

 I was afraid of the noise of the highway as I read many of the reviews complaining about it but I found it much less noisy than expected. It'd say it's similar to sleeping in an apartment next to a busy road (not a highway). But also picked one of the furthest sites, so that might have helped.

reviews.author: Mark G.
reviews.text:
Great location when you’re interested in riding the OATrail.  It’s just unfortunate that some people bring their animals with them. Time them up in the campground while they go hiking and everyone else is forced to endure constant barking. What is the deal with that?  First thing in the morning, last thing at night.

Why should a paying customer without an animal be forced to deal with this kind of abuse? When did we become so antisocial?

Great campsite, not so great campers.

reviews.author: Michelle M.
reviews.text: Campground was absolutely stunning and well maintained. Campground hosts made sure campground rules were being enforced. Facilities were clean.

reviews.author: Douglas  L.
reviews.text: Beautiful setting, clean sites and friendly camp host.  Plenty to do right from the campground.

reviews.author: William L.
reviews.text:
Great basecamp for exploring the national park.  Bathrooms were very clean and there's access to dumpsters which is very convenient.  Less than an hour drive to Forks or Port Angelas areas if you need to stop by a full grocery store.

The lake is beautiful, easy to walk down to the water and boat ramp with an inflatable or a quick drive to ramp if you're feeling lazy.

reviews.author: Corey L.
reviews.text: Perfect as always! Camp host was amazing!

reviews.author: Irene A.
reviews.text: It was spacious enough to fit 2 tents (1 for 8 people and 1 for 4 people). Very close to the lake, and the amenities were pretty clean!

reviews.author: Alejandro S.
reviews.text: We loved the park it was very well kept and very clean!! the bathrooms were pretty clean as well and the location next to the lake is great

reviews.author: Judith R.
reviews.text: Nice campground, clean bathrooms.  Little close to the road and there is some road noise.  Not horrible.

reviews.author: Shawna S.
reviews.text: The perfect spot tucked off in the forest.

reviews.author: Claire B.
reviews.text: Bathrooms were very clean I highly recommend one of the walk in spots near the water. One of my favorite sites Ive been to.

reviews.author: Robert I.
reviews.text: Location is extremely hard to beat. Nice walking paths throughout the campground linking different loops, bathrooms/fresh water, and down to the lake. Store is also right next to the lake for convenience. Campsites are good sizes with plenty of space from your neighbors. Stay here, you won’t regret it!

reviews.author: Rachel L.
reviews.text: Just a Big Wow!

reviews.author: James W.
reviews.text: Nice campground, not too big, with access to the ODT for biking/walking and water activities via boat launch area.  Facilities are fairly well maintained.  Cell coverage (t-mobile) is spotty unless you head down to the beach.  Too many trees for starlink.

reviews.author: Rachel L.
reviews.text:
Beautiful camping with a extraordinaire Forest. The Lake is so beautiful. 
We do hear noise traffic but it is worthed. 
We cannot wait to come back. 
Fantastic!!

reviews.author: Christi C.
reviews.text: Clean, maintained sites with beautiful vegetation.

reviews.author: Joshua P.
reviews.text: We had one of the walk in sites and it was really loud.  I read the reviews of people complaining about the highway noise and thought they were  exaggerating.  Like how bad bad could it be?  I'm not a picky person and deaf in one ear but the campground is at the bottom of a hill and the engine brake noise is quite impressive.  It slows down between 10pm and 5am, but I would look elsewhere if sleeping under an overpass on I5  doesn't sound appealing...  My child slept great.

reviews.author: Shane G.
reviews.text: Great location, well maintained and extraordinary views of the lake. I bike packed through the area and arrived at night in a heavy downpour. There is a small sign off the Discovery trail that marks a small path leading to a road that leads to the campground. If you see this sign follow the path that will lead to a small dirt road then head north. The campground is up the road 1/2 mile or so (very difficult to see the sign at night and the trail looks like a hiking trail). If you miss the turn off there is another opportunity to rejoin the road to the north- I was lucky enough to see a red marker light on a bridge that led me to the road. Great place for sure- should not be a problem to find the road during the day.

reviews.author: Leah D.
reviews.text: This place is gorgeous! The campsites are great but there is no shower at all. It would be 5 stars if there was a way to bathe.

reviews.author: Ivan B.
reviews.text: Good campground on the lake with clean bathrooms.

reviews.author: Greg W.
reviews.text:
The campground was great- I was backpacking the next day and wanted to get an early start so thought I would spend teh night nearby rather than drive from Seattle,

The ranger was really helpful since I had brought a hamock tent and the site that I had selected online had no trees small enough to use my straps... that means the trees were huge!  Beautiful.  She helped me get resituated in minutes.

I took a walk to get away from the crowds and went fishing (you don't need a license to fish in the national park, but I carried it anyways).  Later in the evening I took a 1-mile walk on the trail and it was quiet and beautiful and heard tons of birds but they are ellusive.

Remember that the little store nearby has VERY limited items.

reviews.author: Alexandria W.
reviews.text: My campsite was near the trail down to the lake which was stunning! The facilities were all clean, only downside I had was that there is no soap in the bathrooms. Bring your own soap from home to clean your hands. The campground was quiet, and had lots of little trails to explore the area. There’s a boat ramp nearby that my friends and I walked to one evening and looked at all the stars. I would stay here again in the future.

reviews.author: Henry J.
reviews.text: Great site near the water. Great location if you're trying to catch all parts of the park as it's centrally located. Just be ready to take some longer beautiful drives to see sites as Olympic is just that big of a park.

reviews.author: Rebecca M.
reviews.text: I have camped here several times and love this campground, especially in the spring and fall when its less crowded. None of the campsites are private, but there is a good amount of space between sites so that they don't feel crowded. The campsite is surrounded by gorgeous large trees, and is only a short walk to a clean restroom. The lake is exquisitely clear (bring a paddleboard!) and the bike trail running behind the lake feels wild and secluded. We stayed 3 nights this trip, and we had a barred owl call and fly over our campsite around 10pm each night. It was magical.

reviews.author: Katelynn P.
reviews.text: It was an amazing experience! The bathrooms were brightly lit and super clean. The people were kind and helpful. Didn’t have a chance to check out the campsite store, but the lake was crystal clear and beautiful!

reviews.author: John N.
reviews.text: Beautiful spot and grat campground hosts.

reviews.author: Heather M.
reviews.text: Spectacular lake, scenery and don’t miss the stars at night!

reviews.author: Maya K.
reviews.text: Beautiful lakeside campsite! Clean bathrooms too. Really enjoyed our stay here!

reviews.author: Ted M.
reviews.text: Wonderful place!  Very clean and the scenery was really beautiful.

reviews.author: Gyuyeon H.
reviews.text: I would recommend checking out Fairholme campground. Lake Crescent is beautiful.

reviews.author: Philip K.
reviews.text: Fairholm was in the top 5 campgrounds I’ve stayed at. The proximity and access to the lake cannot be underestimated if you want to swim or otherwise spend time on the water. Great location for accessing hurricane or other parts of the park, too. Facilities and sites are great.

reviews.author: Matthew E.
reviews.text: Campground is pretty, but can be very noisy, you can hear 101 from across the lake. Most sites are very unlevel. The description for our site said "slight grade". We have a short 24ft MH and it was 1.5 feet out of level. Campground hosts were MIA.

reviews.author: gemma t.
reviews.text: Very clean, well maintained. I stayed there because it was the closest campground to Ozette triangle. it worked great.

reviews.author: Donald M.
reviews.text: Beautiful area and enjoyed our stay

reviews.author: Philip C.
reviews.text: We camped in the walk-in loop. There is no privacy and they are small. But we lucked out and no one was camped on our level. It was a Tuesday night in late September. It met our needs nicely. 5 old men with 5 tents. We used 2 adjacent sites.

reviews.author: Joey B.
reviews.text:
If you like clean bathrooms and campsites and a very pretty and accessible lake and don't mind noise, this campground will be perfect for you. If you're looking for any amount of privacy and peace and quiet, look elsewhere. The highway noise is shockingly loud at the walk-in campsites down by the lake, and even on a Sunday, Monday and Tuesday, we heard big logging trucks and other vehicles by all night. There were little kids playing in the lake near our campsite until super late and being very rowdy. We also had neighbors in the camp next to us who watched movies on their laptop at full volume until 2 am, despite us politely asking them to turn down the volume (they didn't and then acted like we were the rude ones for asking). 

The lake is gorgeous and perfect for paddle boarding and swimming and would make a lovely place to hang out for the day. However the noise level and "type" of campers this one attracts is likely to displease folks who are used to the peace and quiet of dispersed or remote camping. Flush toilets sure are nice, though :)

reviews.author: Daisy Y.
reviews.text: This was a great place to set-up as "home base" for the few days I was at ONP. The short walk to Lake Crescent made for some great sunrise views. In addition, the restrooms had hot water! Site 37 was very close to the restroom and trash dumpster, in case proximity to those are important to you.

reviews.author: Maya T.
reviews.text: Site 88 is amazing! Right on the water and the walk down is totally worth it. Bathrooms are clean and well kept.

reviews.author: Apolonia M.
reviews.text: Campsites were very small. No space to put the tent other than the driveway.

reviews.author: Mei Z.
reviews.text: the camp facility is well maintained, campsite with great view of the Crescent Lake.  It was quite noisy from passing cars across the lake.

reviews.author: Karen A.
reviews.text: Beautiful lovely campground next to Lake Crescent

reviews.author: Nathan E.
reviews.text: Had a 4 night stay at the campground and aside from the site having a little slant, it was a great stay!  The lake is beautiful and I would definitely camp here again!

reviews.author: Karla P.
reviews.text: It was great....quiet, with lots of places to find solitude along the lake.

reviews.author: Victoria L.
reviews.text: Gorgeous walks around campground with lovely views of lake. Decent bathrooms, at least not smelly and fairly clean. Set in the temperate rainforest. Just lovely.

reviews.author: McKenna L.
reviews.text: The campground was great! Each site spot felt private. I loved the little trails down to the water. Had a great swim! I will definitely be back.

reviews.author: cory c.
reviews.text: Lovely setting, with swimmable Crescent Lake.  But the campground is very near Highway 101, with lots of traffic, especially the logging trucks with their Jake Brakes, that start roaring down the road at 5 in the morning.  That is a deal breaker for me.  I would not stay there again.

reviews.author: Megan D.
reviews.text: This campground is easy to get to, has a beautiful view and access to Lake Crescent. I stayed at one of the walk in sites which was easy to find. The parking was clear and the campsite is organized and clean. You can hear the cars going by on the nearby road but this was otherwise a perfect spot!

reviews.author: Emily T.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground, good bathrooms, easy to navigate.

reviews.author: Darren O.
reviews.text: we enjoyed site 53. It's close to the bathroom, water and has great views of the lake. The road noise is bad from all the sites that face the lake. But the forest and lake views are worth it

reviews.author: Catherine  S.
reviews.text: The campsite was extremely small and misleading. It looked like we had access to the lake from the pictures on the site and we weren’t anywhere near the water. The bathroom didn’t even have hand soap. No one working there to help and even the camp host were ghost. Lake was still beautiful

reviews.author: Solomon C.
reviews.text: The mini trail/pathway to the lake is about 50 feet from this specific campground. The bathroom is a short walk away behind the campsite. Very peaceful and VERY quiet during my stay. Perfect place to bring a chair and enjoy sunrise/sunset by Lake Crescent on their little pocket viewpoints along the trail. You can see specks of blue water through the trees, which was very beautiful. This campsite is elevated from where you park so its not private as the picnic table pretty much gives you view of everyone else's campsite when looking towards the lake. Otherwise, it was a nice stay and had all the basic needs that every campground usually has.

reviews.author: Manasa K.
reviews.text: ITs a good site with flushable toilets

reviews.author: Dan B.
reviews.text: Site ten had an incline. It was difficult to sleep. Other than that site is an excellent location

reviews.author: Christine C.
reviews.text: The campground itself was beautiful, however, the spot we were in towards the end of the lake, made it absolutely impossible to sleep. The large trucks and logging truck trucks were nonstop. We ended up leaving at about 5 AM so we could go sleep in the car somewhere.

reviews.author: Isaac P.
reviews.text: Very cool spot with a great view of the lake! If you’re an experienced camper then these sites may be kinda close together/crowded. These sites are perfect if you’re just getting into camping but still want a little privacy! This place is also very close to the most popular trails. We will be back!

reviews.author: Julien L.
reviews.text: Great campground, nice path to have access to the lake. If you need services, go by the deck.

reviews.author: Emily B.
reviews.text: This was a lovely campground. It was close to the beach, but tucked away and quiet. As with every NPS campground we stayed at on our trip, we were pleasantly surprised how clean everything was, particularly the bathrooms. Well worth the cost!

reviews.author: marissa w.
reviews.text: Clean bathrooms, clean campsite, gorgeous lake views and easy access. Will continue coming back year after year..

reviews.author: Caleb C.
reviews.text: Really cool campsites.

reviews.author: Valeriia S.
reviews.text: Nice place to stay

reviews.author: Rebecca H.
reviews.text: Great location and campsites.  One downfall was noise from the 101 at night could be heard.  Overall, a great experience!

reviews.author: Daniel S.
reviews.text: Clean and well taken care of campground. Slightly sloped site was a little challenging at first. Access to lake’s small western shore beach. Next to 101. Beautiful area.

reviews.author: Michael B.
reviews.text: The campground was well-maintained and overall a fun experience. My only concern, surprising to me, was how empty it seemed, given how reserved it was supposed to be and how difficult it was to even secure the spot I had. It feels like there could be a better system for releasing unconfirmed reservations the day of, so those spots don’t sit unused..

reviews.author: Chris K.
reviews.text: Bathrooms were clean, campground was lovely. Can’t wait to come back!

reviews.author: Nicole B.
reviews.text: We snagged one of the late release sites - which went within 1 minute of release! Site 4 was decent with two nice areas for a giant tent and a tiny tent. The only drawback at this site was being close to the always-on bathroom lights. Overall, this is a well-kept campground with beautiful trees, clean and functional bathrooms, dishwashing station, and a solid swimming "beach" (by PNW standards) where the water is far warmer than the glacial-fed rivers or the ocean! The walk-in sites are sweet if you are traveling on the lighter side, have backpack gear, or don't mind a little exercise. We prefer less crowded campgrounds, but it's hard to beat this CG location for proximity as a jumping off site for the park. It's popularity indicates how badly they need at least another one or two in the area.

reviews.author: Mauri S.
reviews.text: Our experience at Fairholme  Campground was pleasant; however, it must be said that this is not a quiet and peaceful camping experience. The road traffic is ridiculously loud both day and night! Also, the camp host were never to be seen.  May want to spend some time sitting out around your camper, being available and talking to people. I’m pretty sure this is what you’re supposed to be doing.  Never once saw them during my whole visit, while walking by their space at least 20 times.  Also, the bathrooms were not kept that clean, and unfortunately people were washing their dishes in the bathroom sink. 😳. Lake Crescent is the most beautiful, perfect and pristine lake I have ever visited. If you’re lucky enough to be there during the warm summer – the swimming is exceptional.

reviews.author: George E.
reviews.text: Great location being close to many activities. Disappointed that campfires were not allowed.

reviews.author: Valerie M.
reviews.text: Fairholme was a great campground.  The bathrooms were clean, there was always soap and an electric outlet, and despite not having showers we could walk to Lake Crescent and go for a swim.  The close proximity of the Camp store made it easy to pick up any supplies without having to get in the car.  We were confused that there was no check-in process and our last name wasn't on the sign post by our site, but it appears that checking in isn't required as long as you have a valid reservation.  I would highly recommend staying here.

reviews.author: Lance S.
reviews.text: The campground is situated on a hillside, so be careful about selecting your site as many are unsuitable for RVs.  Many sites are OK for small to medium sized RVs, but not many for larger ones.  Not much space or privacy between sites.  Lovely area, the lake is beautiful and a must do is the Spruce Railroad trail that goes along the northwestern shore of the lake.

reviews.author: Gretchen C.
reviews.text: The bathrooms were very nice for NP bathrooms. We got rained out even though it was August ☹️

reviews.author: Ben M.
reviews.text:
This is an ok campground, but was my least favorite of the four I stayed in at Olympic National Park.  The site is a little small, and while I found a couple options for my 2 man tent, anything bigger would feel cramped.   Unless you do one of the walk in sites with a lake view there’s really nothing memorable about this campground.  Do not book this site if you have a van or rooftop camper.   The parking spot is on a pretty decent incline.  

Lastly, this is probably the closest major campground in the park to Seattle.  That plus the draw of the lake means more of a party vibe and kids than I prefer.   It did finally quiet down at night, but it just wasn’t the atmosphere I prefer.

reviews.author: mark s.
reviews.text: beautiful setting, campsites pretty tight

reviews.author: Jong H.
reviews.text: Lots of mosquitos. The restroom sink were filled with small black insects.

reviews.author: John K.
reviews.text: Great location campground.  A little dated, but has the basics.

reviews.author: Jonathan M.
reviews.text: Great site!  The best part is that you can walk down to the lake on an easy footpath. From there, a path will take you to the beach area. Or you have an easy spot to jump into the lake a short walk from the site. Bathrooms are a short walk uphill. The lake is beautiful!

reviews.author: Jon N.
reviews.text: Beautiful setting and experience. We had plenty of space on our site (76) which was slightly sloped but comfortable. The only negative would be the highway noise at night.

reviews.author: Yasmine B.
reviews.text: Very nice campsite, regret amenities, and a good atmosphere. Awesome

reviews.author: Jacquelyn K.
reviews.text: The walk in sites are on top of each other. Campers were highly inconsiderate of their light and sound after quiet hours. Camp hosts were no where in sight to enforce these rules. Highway noise was awful. We left a night earlier than expected.

reviews.author: Katrina G.
reviews.text:
Loved our time!  Spot 54 was pretty small and butts right up against walk in campers. 
Spot 58 was beautiful and larger than most.  
Weather was great-  good access to the beautiful lake on several trails.  
Watch out for fire bans in August. 
Side note: I really think it Seems so lame to have bans in designated fire rings.  I’d be curious to see the statistics on forest fires started or exacerbated from national park campgrounds’ fire rings.  Fire bans in dispersed camping for sure.  I know not the campgrounds fault- but maybe something they can think about in the future.

reviews.author: chloe h.
reviews.text: This was a beautiful campground and we had lots of space at our campsite. The restrooms were clean.

reviews.author: Jennifer K.
reviews.text: The sites are very small and close together so very little privacy, and some noise from other groups. Bathrooms were clean, but there is no soap at the sinks so be sure to bring your own. Otherwise, great experience, resources easy to find. Some occasional spotty cell service, and were able to drive to service nearby to keep tabs on potential campfire bans. Centrally located so that you can access all the OP has to offer from this base of operations.

reviews.author: Samantha D.
reviews.text:
Campsite was beautiful. Went with site 86, right on the water. I researched on forums ahead of time and that is definitely my top pick as long as you don’t mind the walk to the site. You can walk into the water from there instead of having to take this really long path down to the docks. One of the negatives though is that the sites are all very densely packed and they are spread out across different leveled tiers, meaning there are hills between each level. Site 86 is at the very bottom - three levels down. Not ideal at all. Especially for bringing your camping gear to the site. Also we arrived in the dark and it was extremely difficult to find. There should really be a map there. There may have been up near the bathrooms but I’m not sure. But mind you, the bathrooms are a fourth level up so to get there you have to climb three hills. The bigger two are paved but I have a bad knee so it was difficult. To get from site 86 to the parking lot where our spot was reserved you had to go up one really steep hill and then a smaller hill to get to it. 
My suggestion for a second choice after seeing it in person would be 76 as there’s a bit of privacy but it’s not on the lake so you have a bit of a walk to get to the docks to access the water. Also there was no soap in the bathroom fyi so bring your own. But they were very clean which was good.

reviews.author: Anneliese A.
reviews.text: Lovely campsite right on the shore of Lake Crescent. Yes, you can hear the traffic on 101 and the trail up to the restrooms is steep, but it's still a really nice place to camp. This walk-in site was right on the lake, which was really nice. The ground did slope a little, so we made sure to set up our tents so that our feet were pointing downhill. Beautiful view.

reviews.author: Robert S.
reviews.text: Good campground with bathrooms

reviews.author: Sohee K.
reviews.text: Clean restroom. Lake view is amazing!

reviews.author: Abigail E.
reviews.text: I hate to say it as I don’t want to campground to become overrun, but there’s a reason it’s so difficult to book at this campground. It’s absolutely gorgeous and the facilities were better than others in the ONP. I hope to be able to stay here again many summers in the future. The site itself was lovely and didn’t feel cramped or stacked on top of one another.

reviews.author: Kelly F.
reviews.text: Sol doc falls hike was our favorite; as were the trails around the crescent lodge. Hoh rainforest was dimmed by the 2.5hr car wait followed by only 2mi of trails once you get in—plan carefully!

reviews.author: Amanda R.
reviews.text: Great campground and beautiful campsite

reviews.author: Desiree W.
reviews.text: Fairholme Campground is set in tall trees with lots or undergrowth separating campsites, on the shore of lovely Lake Crescent. The facilities (bathroom, water spigot etc) are nice and the campsite was great. Despite there being many sites in multiple loops, the campground was overall very quiet and peaceful!

reviews.author: Tracy L.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsites and access to Crescent Lake and Hurricane Ridge was close by.

reviews.author: Erick Z.
reviews.text: Beautiful lake and nice facilities.

reviews.author: Suzanne B.
reviews.text: Gorgeous lake facing campsite.  The restrooms were sparkling clean. Our walk-in site shared a bear box with several other sites. It worked out just fine.  Great little trail behind the campground. General store had all the basics.

reviews.author: Marianne S.
reviews.text: Lovely campsite, walk-in #79, a short walk from parking. Partial view of the gorgeous lake, short walk to beach, camp store, and docks. You can hear the road noise from the highway but also plenty of birdsong. Totally worth it. Hope to return and stay longer.

reviews.author: Paulina G.
reviews.text: Very clean, quick and easy access to restrooms and potable water. Our site (1,A) was a short walk away from the boating zone, very big and clean! The only downside is that it was pretty noticeable inclined.

reviews.author: Regina C.
reviews.text:
The good: location was good for visiting north side of ONP, warm water in bathroom sinks was nice
The bad: bring your own toilet paper-there was some in the A loop bathroom when I arrived but it was empty that afternoon and never replenished by the time I left late the next day. Also be prepared for a walk up or down hill, and a wait when it’s busy: there are 90 campsites and only three bathrooms, and the one I used only had two stalls.
My site didn’t have this problem, but beware if you get a spot near a bathroom. The toilets  have an automated pressure flush that is very loud. I felt so bad when I used the bathroom in the middle of the night!

reviews.author: Cheryle G.
reviews.text:
Great location.
We stayed in site 81 the Picnic table was in bad shape. Bench seat broken and proped up with wood blocks. Table top had chunks missing, really needs to be replace.

reviews.author: Sarah W.
reviews.text: N

reviews.author: Grace H.
reviews.text: I stayed here to hike the Hurricane Ridge next day, the view was incredible and I wish I could stay longer.  The parking was on a slope but luckily a kind neighbor was able to help.  Lots mosquitoes as its next to lake so protect yourself properly.  The facilities are clean.  I highly recommend this site.

reviews.author: Michael H.
reviews.text: Stayed at 21B, set up two large tents, one on designated pad, other on driveway. Plus 2 vehicles. Decent privacy, and hwy noise sometimes annoying but knew about noise prior.  Restrooms clean and in great condition.  Swam in Lake Cresent daily.  The store there rents kayaks too.  Great location to visit many of the popular areas.

reviews.author: Caitlin C.
reviews.text: Such a beautiful campground in walking distance to the lake. Some people had issues with the proximity to the road but it didn't bother us. Whenever I return to Olympic NP, I will stay here longer!

reviews.author: Anand P.
reviews.text: What a special place! By far the highlight of our trip.

reviews.author: Lucia V.
reviews.text: Just WOW!!! This spot was BREATHTAKING! We have zero cons. You are camping in one of the most beautiful places in the US. Clear blue waters, super clean bathrooms/showers. Easy access to everything and then some. Sure spot isn’t a flat surface but i mean, it’s camping for a reason. This is no hotel or clamping place. Respect all nature and it will treat you with the same respect. We Will come back again and again for the next years to come!! Thank you to the people who work hard to keep this place beautiful!

reviews.author: Sandeep Reddy P.
reviews.text: All the amenities are well maintained and the site has very good view. However, given that the location is right on the lake, bringing the stuff down to site is a bit of hassle.

reviews.author: Alicia P.
reviews.text:
Very nice campground. We had more than enough room for our 7x7 3 person tent. The sites were a little too close to each other for our liking. It felt like you could easily hear your neighbors conversations to the right and the left. 
The sky at night is really beautiful though, you can see so many stars!

reviews.author: Joshua W.
reviews.text: Campsite 86 is probably the worst of the waterfront campsites because it's small and has a hill right in the center of the campsite so it makes it hard to set anything up.

reviews.author: Meghann C.
reviews.text:
I would never stay here again. Sites were incredibly close, so you have absolutely no privacy. Quiet hours were not enforced, so the first night we had 2 neighboring groups (just a few feet away) up past midnight partying. The second night people were partying on the next loop and had dogs barking for hours, well past quiet hours. It was hard to sleep. Road noise also goes on all night. It can get loud. 

The lake front access is incredibly small and open to the public, so it’s very crowded. Beautiful lake and surrounding areas, but I would rather stay at Sol Duc and explore the lake on my own. 

Overall terrible experience! Do not recommend.

reviews.author: Michael S.
reviews.text: Great site, close to the lake

reviews.author: Michelle P.
reviews.text:
Very busy locations with only 2 bathroom stalls for the ladies in loop B.
There was no hand soap at any point during my stay.

Very noisey from dogs barking, car alarms going off and all the traffic from across the lake. 

The tent sites along the water would have been a nightmare , it looked like ppl were almost camped on top of another, zero privacy and lots of folks walking past their tents.

I wouldn’t stay there again.

reviews.author: Melissa S.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsites overlooking Crescent Lake.

reviews.author: Amy N.
reviews.text: It was a lovely camp site in a beautiful campground. Everyone stuck to the curfew everyone was silent at 10pm. The bathroom where very clean and nice. The campground host was very nice and friendly she came by every evening and do her walk of the grounds. The only downside to the campground was the steep incline to the lake we would just go to the boat ramp instead of walking down the steep trail to the water I was to afraid of hurting my ankel or something. But there isn't anything you could do but use a different trail to the lake. Other than that it was a beautiful time.

reviews.author: Abbey H.
reviews.text: One of our favorite campgrounds ever! Really great location right by the beautiful Crescent Lake! All the sites are super cool and pretty!

reviews.author: Victoria H.
reviews.text: The lake was gorgeous and clear. Campground was clean. Lots of mosquitoes. Water is centrally located on A and C loops so if you are on B loop and the bottom, you are a bit far away. Did I mention mosquitoes?

reviews.author: Taylor K.
reviews.text: I truly enjoyed this campground. The campsites are relatively close to one another, but it still felt like we had privacy. The other campers respected the quiet hours and bathrooms were easy to access/kept clean. I would recommend this location to others, if you can get a spot.

reviews.author: Allen W.
reviews.text: We stayed in a wonderful walk-in site right on the lake shore. Very picturesque. Sites are a little close together and there is a steep walk up to the bathrooms, but totally amazing scenery.

reviews.author: Collin N.
reviews.text: great site, no complaints!

reviews.author: Fred S.
reviews.text: lovely sites--steep hills within campground, nice bathrooms, great beach access,

reviews.author: Rhonda H.
reviews.text: Well maintained campground, friendly host.

reviews.author: Hailey O.
reviews.text: Needs more sun. Campsites were cold and windy. Campsites were also much smaller than expected and shown in the pictures

reviews.author: Wendy P.
reviews.text: Great location. Clean sites and bathrooms. Staff offered hiking tips. Eclectic campers: lots of kids (yes‼️), someone getting tattooed, a DJ spinning quietly lakeside.

reviews.author: Tim B.
reviews.text: Site driveway isn’t level. Not great for van camping.

reviews.author: MARGARET M.
reviews.text: Beautiful, peaceful campground on the lake.  Hot & cold runny water and flush toilets was appreciated.  Would come back again.

reviews.author: Sarah H.
reviews.text: Beautiful, peaceful, and clean campsite. Excellent location between Port Angeles and Forks on lake Cresent. Good hikes, activities on the lake, and watching stars on the dock all within a short walk or drive away.

reviews.author: Bill F.
reviews.text: Campsites under the big trees are wonderful! The campground is sloped, but each campsite is level. The bathroom was clean and relatively new. Nice experience!

reviews.author: Laurel C.
reviews.text: Beautiful, peaceful, clean bathrooms.

reviews.author: Julet B.
reviews.text: Loved this campsite. Would come back again. Great view of the water!!

reviews.author: Jennifer  S.
reviews.text: Great location!

reviews.author: Amber F.
reviews.text:
What an absolute oasis! Not only is the campground incredibly well maintained, but our host (Sue) was an absolute delight. She was a well of information and kindness. 
The bathrooms were clean, but no soap or hand sanitizer is provided so bring your own! 
Our spot was the closets walk in from the lot, but still has an INCREDIBLE view. Even with a tent in front of us (77) every night we stayed, we could still clearly see the lake. 
The walk down the lake is somewhat steep in spots but it truly a quick little walk to go swim, get to the camp store, or fish! 
We did have some obnoxious neighbors who used the campsite as their personal bar hang out until the wee hours. We spoke to our camp host after 2 nights of it, and she reminded me to come see her if they refuse to quiet down during quiet hours.

reviews.author: Danielle K.
reviews.text:
Gorgeous campground, it was our favorite spot of the trip! We were almost completely surrounded by mossy trees and gorgeous leaves, with the lake only a few yards away. The volunteer at the campground was very friendly, she welcomed us, gave us maps, helped us with tips and recommendations. The campsite was quiet and peaceful even though it was completely full, with plenty of bathrooms and space for everyone. 

We ended up staying a few night here as a central location while driving out during the day to experience other parts of the park and surrounding area, including a whale-watching tour out of Port Angeles, and drive and hike up Hurricane Ridge, a hike to Devil's Punchbowl, Marymere Falls, and a few other places in between. We then moved on to a couple of other campgrounds as we made our way through the park, but we all agreed of the campgrounds we stayed at this trip, this was our favorite. 

Next time we visit Olympic, we will definitely spend another few nights here!

reviews.author: Susan S.
reviews.text: Campground is nice within the trees. Pick your site carefully if you have a van or camper. Most don't seem to be level. We have a van and our site was not level. Campground is right on Lake Cresent and the surrounding area is beautiful.

reviews.author: Pamela K.
reviews.text: We arrived and got to the site but it was not conducive to our 24 ft motor home.  Where we needed to park it was narrow and on a large mound.  We had to leave and find another campground!  Wish we could have stayed!

reviews.author: lisa l.
reviews.text: Clean site near lake. Restrooms were clean and had easy access.  Rangers were helpful and friendly. We will go again

reviews.author: Taylor S.
reviews.text: We love camping at fairholme. The campground is well maintained and quiet, and the lake is perfect for warm weather recreation.

reviews.author: Sam H.
reviews.text: Really awesome place for the summer. The store by the camp actually has a lot of what you need to camp, you could easily show up and just get food/snacks from there. Absolutely beautiful lake

reviews.author: Peyton F.
reviews.text: What a magical experience! This may be the best campsite I've ever gotten to stay at. There was so much room, close enough walk to the bathrooms, and the views were beautiful. Will definitely be recommending to all.

reviews.author: Travis M.
reviews.text: Great camp ground especially if you wanna take the boat out on the lake. Nice clean bathrooms and a spot to clean dishes outside.

reviews.author: Mischa D.
reviews.text: Great campground! Everything was as described. Great store in walking distance for anything you might need or forgotten.

reviews.author: Lori P.
reviews.text: So green and nice bathrooms. The Spruce Railroad Trail was beautiful along the lake. A definite must do.

reviews.author: Brian M.
reviews.text: Beautiful place to camp! Because of how gorgeous Olympic national park is, just about every site was beautiful. We wanted one with a view of the lake and chose site 60. While a decent choice, upon getting to the campground and seeing other sites. I wish someone would update some of the photos on recreation.gov, with more than one view of each campsite. Great base of operations for seeing a lot of of the popular attractions on the north side of the peninsula. Even the walk up to the bathrooms was gorgeous! Lol!

reviews.author: Rachel S.
reviews.text:
Campground is great. Lake and docks are within an easy stroll. Bathrooms are clean; no showers, but flush toilets. 

This campsite was a short, steep walk-to from parking (<50ft). Small, shared bear box was available a short walk away. Campsite overlooks the lake through a few trees and is very shady and level.

The only reason I couldn't rate it 5 stars is due to the amount of road noise from across the lake. Thankfully, it does ease off later at night, but I wouldn't say this site qualified as "quiet". Still peaceful overall, though.

reviews.author: Mackenzie J.
reviews.text: The campground is beautiful but at this particular site the picnic table was entirely unusable as it was broken in half and rotted away. This created a significant inconvenience that was not expected and made our trip less than enjoyable in that aspect. We hadn’t brought our own table because the site is advertised to have a picnic table and we were not advised otherwise. The park ranger was aware of the state of the picnic table and still did not think to relay that information to the people paying for the site.

reviews.author: Jennifer B.
reviews.text: Campsite was nice but if you are sleeping in your car this spot was a bad choice. Car spot is not flat. And the dumpster is too close. This wasn’t ideal. I’d choose a different spot.

reviews.author: Kristie C.
reviews.text: Site #89 is beautiful. However, it is a horrible walk downhill from your parking spot. Actually it is a combo of downhills so going up is awful. Like almost vertical. So either dont pick this site unless you are bringing nothing in or drive up to the boat launch and walk your stuff to the site. That way is flat but unknown as an option. Would not stay at a waterfront site here again because of this.  Campground itself is nice with clean bathrooms.

reviews.author: Barbora S.
reviews.text:
Love this campground by beautiful Lake Crescent. Hiking, biking, boating and swimming. 
Olympic Discovery Railroad Trail - along the lake’s north shore - is ideal for families with kids, but also for all cyclists who want to avoid dangerous part of US101 (trail is paved road, but no motorized traffic allowed). 
Great base for daily trips to other places in Olympic NP. Small store by the main road has fire wood and basic supplies.
There is almost no cell coverage and no showers at the campground. Restrooms are kept clean. Drinking water is available.

reviews.author: Emmy C.
reviews.text: really loved the place, would love to go back again.

reviews.author: Gabriel H.
reviews.text: Fairholme and the surround area are always epic. Facilities were clean, and the grounds are in great condition. Perfect location from a Crescent and Sol Duc getaway.

reviews.author: stephen m.
reviews.text:
The walk-to site I unfortunately reserved was really bad, because it was tiny and everybody walks right past/thru your site to access the other lakeshore sites or the lake itself. The site next door is so close you can hear your neighbors pass gas as they take a leak in the lake.

Be warned!

reviews.author: Collin J.
reviews.text: The campground was great and the lake is just breathtaking. Sadly, our neighbors pulled into the spot at 11pm and stayed up drinking and partying until 3am. We didn't get good sleep, but that was only because of our neighbors and not the site itself!

reviews.author: Jennifer  F.
reviews.text: We loved it here! Such a beautiful view. It's on a pretty steep cliff edge, so you have to walk up/over then down different paths to get to the water. Keep dogs leashed so they don't go over the edge and watch kids carefully. We would definitely come back!

reviews.author: Brandon L.
reviews.text: Nice campsites next to Lake Crescent. Boat launch is a short walk or quick drive since it's next to the campground.  When the campsites are full they are kinda close to each other but it really isn't a problem. I camped twice at two different sites and enjoyed both. There are some sites that are first come first serve so the campground wasn't full either time I went.  Enjoyed kayaking on the lake, I will be back for sure.

reviews.author: Colin F.
reviews.text: This is a great campground with easy access to Lake Crescent for watersports, the Spruce Railroad Trail for bicycling or walking, and myriad of hiking opportunities within a few miles.  Since this campground is across the lake from Hwy 101 you will hear traffic; if camping a tent you may sleep better with ear plugs.

reviews.author: Leia R.
reviews.text: Wonderful campground. Beautiful lake, lovely wooded campsites. Clean bathrooms. VERY full campground. We were there the third week of September on a Monday and it was completely full.

reviews.author: Sherri W.
reviews.text: We had a nice spot on a beautiful lake.  We enjoyed riding bikes on the nearby bike trail.

reviews.author: Michael S.
reviews.text:
Site Loop A #8 was not as represented and nothing like photo. Advertised as pull thru site 45’. Picnic table has been placed in middle of drive. This is a heavy concrete table. I request refund. 

I recommend staff review the site and revise their information. Also, harvest hosts were not available. Their sites were vacant.

reviews.author: Ashlee M.
reviews.text: Great location, so much to do at the lake!

reviews.author: Ryoko A.
reviews.text:
#30B is a pretty small site, it says maximum 8 but comfortably fits 1 or 2 people, and 3 people would be the maximum in my opinion.  
The camping table looks down over the site and the drive roads, so it doesn't feel very private. Otherwise, the campsite and restroom are very clean, with a nice rainforest, and it is a beautiful campsite.

reviews.author: Mar G.
reviews.text: Lovely place, found it while we were heading south and decided to go through Avenue of the Giants and it was such a godsend, waking up under such amazing trees! Staff was helpful and campers respectful and polite, I want to come back !

reviews.author: Piper C.
reviews.text: So pretty. Somewhat close together and highways right there but worth it

reviews.author: Bill S.
reviews.text: Fairhome is a very popular campground that is difficult to book unless you log in to recreation.gov at just the right time.  Its a nice campground but isn't really anything special which leads me to wonder why it books so rapidly.  Also, it would be good if there were more restrooms for the number of people who camp there.

reviews.author: Irina B.
reviews.text: good camping. warm water in the toilet. the only downside was that we couldn't hammer in the tent stakes at site 54c. very hard ground.

reviews.author: Bry G.
reviews.text: Really beautiful campground with nice, clean bathrooms! Some cell service. Did not swim in the lake due to a sign near the bathrooms in Loop A warning about a rash caused by parasites.  But very beautiful to look at. Would stay here again!

reviews.author: Amelia M.
reviews.text: Absolutely beautiful site with clean facilities and respectful patrons. Would highly recommend!

reviews.author: Knox G.
reviews.text: This not actually a level site for a van— the pull-through would probably work better for a small trailer that has some jacks to level it, but then also the rest of the site is above the trailer, it's a bit awkward. So, maybe this would just be a better tent site. I would not take this site again for our camper van.

reviews.author: Raimunda D.
reviews.text: Way too expensive for camping right next to HWY 101!

reviews.author: Richard P.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground in a stunning rainforest close to a gorgeous lake. Would highly recommend.

reviews.author: Olivia S.
reviews.text: The campsite on the water was wonderful and beautiful. Really loved waking up to the lake, and the bathrooms were well maintained with a good wash up station. One complaint is that the site was a little loud with passing traffic and car headlights passing by. Next time would bring earplugs and an eye mask. But still had a wonderful time and grateful I landed a spot thru the cancellation alert system!

reviews.author: Carrie M.
reviews.text: Nice campsite next to a breathtaking lake.

reviews.author: summer h.
reviews.text: We took a 10 day trip from Northern CA to Canada and this was by far our favorite stop. The campground is so clean, quiet and beautiful. Didn’t have to worry about huge animals, bugs or loud street noise. The camp host was super friendly and let us know about the lake access beaches around campsite 59 (super glad he told us that because WOW, was it beautiful down there!) We had to venture out of the park to shower but it wasn’t too far and we needed to get out and explore anyway. We will definitely be back!

reviews.author: Neil P.
reviews.text: Nice campsites near water

reviews.author: Roderick S.
reviews.text: Clean bathroom and great location.

reviews.author: ALEXANDRIA B.
reviews.text: It was beautiful here, just on the lake, and the facilities were good as well. I cannot wait to book this campground again when I go back.

reviews.author: Hung P.
reviews.text: Campground was easy to get to, near the Sol Duc entrance for Olympic National Park, supplies nearby. Being on Lake Crescent was the bees knees of the joint. Site was clean as were the bathroom, nice dish washing area as well.

reviews.author: George A.
reviews.text: Beautiful CG in Olympic National Park.  Great location near the lake.  Some highway noise.

reviews.author: Christopher K.
reviews.text:
Positives: The Lake and surrounding mountains were beautiful. Easy to find campground. Proximity to Sol Duc and Port Angeles. 

Areas of Improvements: bathroom was undersized for campground. Long lines to access during busy times in evening before sunset.  Nearby 101 had 24/7 logging truck activity. The sounds of large trucks accelerating westward up the hill and then gear breaking when coming down eastwards echoed across the lake making for an anxious and unsteady night of sleep. Bring earplugs, especially  if your campsite is near the lake shore.

reviews.author: Nami B.
reviews.text:
Our site had a large parking space but there was no space to pitch a tent. 
There was no evenly flat space for even a small tent. The Parking space was flat and spacious but the ground was too hard to pitch pegs… luckily our 2 person tent was narrow enough to barely fit the space between the parking and bush that was somewhat flat. This site should be clearly noted for a van or RV site, shouldn’t allow tent camping so no one gets disappointed. 
Nice to have easy lake access and small general store by the campground.

reviews.author: Robert P.
reviews.text: Nice clean campground located in the middle of an area rich with activities. The camp hosts were some of the kindest, friendliest and most professional people I have encountered in a long time.

reviews.author: Kristy L.
reviews.text: Someone was at our spot when we arrived, turns out he had a reservation as well. Somehow they double booked us at this site.

reviews.author: Katherine K.
reviews.text: The attendants were always off duty. If you plan to have a nice quiet nights sleep get a hotel. Propane fire pits are permitted when there’s a burn ban. Beautiful space it’s just too bad it's not dispersed. We all had a great time either way.

reviews.author: reagan m.
reviews.text: so amazing and beautiful, everyone is so helpful and it is such a prime location for lake crescent, we were able to hike all over and swim. it is a little crowded and close conditions but no big deal. Maybe they could make it easier to find the walk to sites, there was no signage on where which one was until you came across it.

reviews.author: stephanie s.
reviews.text: convenient location to Lake Crescent

reviews.author: Sara P.
reviews.text: Our site was a nice view of Lake Crescent, but the road noise all night long was pretty loud. Bring your earplugs. Other notes include that you have to walk through other sites to get to this site and while there is a bear box, it's shared. Tent space isn't incredibly flat, but the location was perfect base camp for our activities. From here, we went to Hurricane Ridge, Lake Crescent Lodge, Madison & Marymere Falls, and Sol Duc easily.

reviews.author: Nicole R.
reviews.text:
We had an amazing time at Fairholme! It really is a magical place and one of the most beautiful places i've ever camped at. We stayed in site #85 one of the walk-in spots right on the lake. I was so thrilled to get one of these spots by being up first thing in the morning when the reservations opens up.  

Somethings to know about this site, while its stunning and you are literally right on the water you have to walk up and down a pretty steep hill, I would recommend bringing a wagon for your gear or all your stuff is going to go flying down the hill when you pack to leave like I saw with several others. The site is located right at the entrance of the path down to the lower walk in spots on the lake so there will be people walking right past your site constantly. It would be nice if they oriented the picnic bench on the opposite side of the site instead of it facing directly into the neighboring camp site, kind of awkward. 

Minor things that I easily looked over because we spent most of our time on the shore of the lake with the cute ducks or in the water. The general store was well stocked with a good selection of items too.  We had a fabulous time and can't wait to return and try out one of the other sites!

reviews.author: Yili G.
reviews.text: Gorgeous view

reviews.author: Maria M.
reviews.text:
Site 83 is beautiful and next to the lake. It is shaded, which is nice for hot days. You are right next to a little beach, so you can easily launch from there. The only thing to consider is the site is slanted, so we could not lay flat. The ground is so slanted, things kept rolling down the table. The picnic table looks really old, but served its purpose.

The site is close to the potable water spigot, only a walk up. You have to hike down a bit to get to the site from the parking lot. You have to hike up to the bathroom, but we were not bothered by this.

I have Tmobile and I had about 1-2 bars and 5G the whole time.

reviews.author: Mara  A.
reviews.text: Just about perfect. Sites are spaced a reasonable distance apart, so very private and quiet. Bathrooms were clean. I wish we could have stayed longer and would love to come back.

reviews.author: Melany  S.
reviews.text:
Nice campsite. Running water and flushing toilets. Nice surrounding trails and close access to water ramp. 
It is a bummer to see so many open sites despite showing full on their website. Lucky we were able to snatch a cancelled site reservation.

reviews.author: Leah C.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground. No cell service.

reviews.author: Cuyler C.
reviews.text: The campground is fantastic! It feels very tucked away in the woods, and having access to a little trail for a post-dinner loop and the lake to stick your toes into is just wonderful.

reviews.author: Matt M.
reviews.text: Please hire more rangers and camp hosts.   Boat ramp was filthy with freeloaders camping overnight and dumping waste and trash.   People were speeding through the campground at all hours.

reviews.author: Diane S.
reviews.text: Campground was beautiful, and great location for us.  The lovely setting was diminished somewhat by the small size of the sites and also that most of them are on a slant, and the whole campground is on a hill so it was a workout every trip to the bathroom.  It would probably be hard for older people or people with disabilities to get around, and also makes it so a kid wouldn't be able to ride a bike around.

reviews.author: Jason Y.
reviews.text: Don’t be fooled by the picture. The site is located right next to 2 other sights, with a 3rd just above this site. Great location but extremely crowded

reviews.author: Terri W.
reviews.text: My husband and I have driven by Lake Crescent and the Fairholm store hundreds of times and had never been to the campground. It was soooooo worth it! The beauty was breathtaking.

reviews.author: Mariya S.
reviews.text: I love Lake Crescent and enjoyed our waterfront site #83. Yes, it's a steep walk to the car, but 100% worth it if you want the view and the water access. That said, even if you want to access the water, there are public spots even if you didn't get one of the lakefront sites. There is some noise from highway 101, I wore earplugs at night.

reviews.author: KRISTIN M.
reviews.text: This spot was very quiet at night and had a good amount of room.

reviews.author: KRISTIN M.
reviews.text: Site was small but lovely.   You can hear the road traffic at night which is a bummer.  Very long walk to the site.  Recommend unpacking from the boat ramp and walking the trail along the coastline.

reviews.author: Kiara B.
reviews.text: Nice campground, but firewood is not available at the site if you're arriving later in the day

reviews.author: Matthew A.
reviews.text: Great facilities, amazing location, no cell service, fantastic place

reviews.author: Quoc T.
reviews.text: Big campsite, can fit a 9x14 tent easily. Conveniently located near bathroom, but without too much noise.

reviews.author: Sue S.
reviews.text: Hiking was amazing and Sol Duc Falls was very cool.  :-)  No showers at the camp ground so Sol Duc saved the day.  Most camp sites were bigger and private.  Enjoyed my stay.

reviews.author: Jenny B.
reviews.text: The campground itself is in a very central location and it's beautiful.  Most of the sites were large enough and didn't feel like you were on top of your neighbor.  However, site 84 is one of the smallest sites I saw, and it's very tight being between the trail and the lake.  There really is room for one smaller tent (maybe a 4 person?) and not much else.  We had a few 1 and 2 person backpacking tents and it didn't work for us unfortunately.  If you want to be on the water and around all the action, it would be fine.  It's not exactly close to the bath house either if that's a concern.

reviews.author: Amie G.
reviews.text: Great camp site right next to the lake. Bring bug spray. Mosquitoes are plentiful.

reviews.author: Addie  L.
reviews.text: This particular site abuts another one pretty closely, so we ended up pitching our tent down in the parking area next to our car instead of next to the picnic table. But the facilities were great! Easy access to the bathroom, which was inconsistently stocked but clean, and a pretty campground.

reviews.author: Laura R.
reviews.text: Campground was nice, clean and very shady. The women's restrooms however were quite dirty, primarily the sinks and floors. This may be because it was the 4th of July weekend and it got a lot of traffic.

reviews.author: Mohammed Saju S.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsite.

reviews.author: Lyall A.
reviews.text: Great campground with very helpful rangers (Simon in particular)  Unfortunately very poor weather so didn't get to use much of amenities.

reviews.author: Pankaj C.
reviews.text: Thank you!!

reviews.author: Amanda A.
reviews.text: Hung up our hammocks right next to the water! Not too many bugs (late June) but enough we used our bug nets. Also not too noisy, we slept through the night no issues (but we are heavy sleepers)! Perfect spot for launching our kayak in the morning. There is not a food storage box at this site so keep it in car or share with neighbors. The walk to the bathroom or car for supplies is pretty close, but it is uphill on the way out, so a good idea to only bring down what you need. Fairholme is our favorite campground in Olympic - this was our 4th time staying there!

reviews.author: Anthony O.
reviews.text:
Sites are entirely too close, facilities are dirty. If you want to hear your neighbor snore this is a perfect spot. 

Direct access to the lake but otherwise not a pleasant experience

reviews.author: Holly L.
reviews.text:
The campground itself is beautiful! That view of the lake and easy access to trails is so nice. 

However, that was one of the dirtiest bathrooms I’ve seen at a National Park. No soap, bugs and dirt everywhere. Don’t get me wrong, I camp a lot, and am used to primitive bathrooms. However, this one was super bad and there was no where to set your stuff and no hooks near the sink so getting ready for bed was less than ideal. I left a bar of soap cause luckily I had one from the last hotel we stayed at but honestly one of the worse bathrooms. I hope they clean more consistently in the future!

reviews.author: Victoria A.
reviews.text: I was worried this spot wouldn’t have a great water view  (like 77 & 79) because it was one of the furthest walk in sites from the water and there’s a campsite (77) DIRECTLY in front of us but it was wonderful! I think part of the continuous beautiful view from our spot was that the campers in front of us only set up their tent right before sundown (or later) and left before we were up. Others say at this campground highway noise is a bother but honestly I didn’t notice unless I was directly at the lake front. This spot is conveniently close to the designated parking spot and even closer to the bathrooms. This spot is also only a stones throw away from a water spigot as well. I am in love with this campground and its views from almost every spot!! The only complaint I have is that it’s very difficult to secure a spot during reservation season and it seems half of the walk in campers only stay at their site to sleep and then presumably finish their Olympic national park itinerary during the day. I wish there was a way for people who actually want to stay at their site their entire stay could get “dibs” on the most sought out for spots opposed to those who only sleep at the site and leave. Overall though it was an amazing stay!

reviews.author: Jerold a.
reviews.text: fucking love this place.

reviews.author: dane t.
reviews.text: Great location when visiting olympic national park. camground is clean and quiet, it also next to  lake cresent, make sure you bring your paddle board or kayaks!

reviews.author: Stephanie K.
reviews.text: A lovely campground with access to peaceful, beautiful Lake Crescent, a jewel in the Olympics.  Note, the sites are on a hill sloping down to the lake and there are no showers, so this may not work for some campers.

reviews.author: Elizabeth M.
reviews.text: Out of all the ONP campgrounds I’ve stayed at, this was by far my favorite. Lots of great vegetation and trees and while you’re still next to other campers, you still fully feel like you’re out in nature. Walkable to Fairholme store (although I wish they sold bags of ice!) & close to the railway trail (which would be a great bike ride w kids). We kayaked on the other side of the lake (thru the resort) which was smoother and had rentals available by the hour. Definitely check out Sol Duc hot springs and Marymere waterfall as well!

reviews.author: Claire K.
reviews.text: Such a beautiful campground. Would love better areas to view the lake, but it was a  very natural coast line.  The trees were Magnificent. But facilities were regular campground facilities, and were clean and accessible.

reviews.author: Andrew B.
reviews.text: Well positioned within the park. It's very nice to camp so close to the lake - the little beach there was much less busy than other parts of the park, so it was often easy to get time (nearly) to yourself. Restroom facilities were fair. The only downside for me was the proximity to the road; since the main road runs along the other side of the lake, I would often hear traffic passing through the park.

reviews.author: Peter D. R.
reviews.text: National Park camping on Crescent Lake - near some of the Olympic National park trails/sites (Sol Duc hot springs, Elwha Valley, and Hurricane Ridge).  The campground was fine, but one thing we were used to with National Park campgrounds was more of a Ranger presence, whether that be with a small on-site visitor center or ranger lead programs.  There was a ranger who helped us change sites, but otherwise it felt more on the outskirts of the park rather than inside it.  Other than that - we enjoyed the serenity of Crescent Lake, and the facilities were clean.

reviews.author: Jesse C.
reviews.text: Beautiful tall trees  and a lovely clear lake are the natural wonders that grace this campground but unfortunately, it’s only the natural beauty that carry this campground.  The design of the campground and amenities are quite poor.  Fairholme is built into a fairly steep hillside and sites are stacked closely so that our camp site was directly above another, offering both parties little privacy.   There are also no showers at the campground, making it hard to stay there for longer than a few days.  I’ve stayed at a number of National Park campgrounds and this one was just Ok.  Here’s hoping they get some more many for their park to upgrade their facilities.  It’s not stopping the crowds from doing but it holding back the experience of camping at this campground.

reviews.author: Jordan B.
reviews.text: We loved our campsite, it was quiet and felt very private. The campground is absolutely gorgeous with easy access to Olympic national park and lots of other hiking too.

reviews.author: Morika S.
reviews.text: Beautiful place

reviews.author: Jordan W.
reviews.text: Bathrooms were clean. I'm from Iowa so I'm used to a lot of bugs and they were no bugs here which was amazing.

reviews.author: Christian D.
reviews.text: Beautiful place.  No showers though.

reviews.author: Shirley G.
reviews.text: I enjoyed how quiet this campground was.  Maps don't indicate the change in elevation in the campground or which sites are tippy, so be careful when choosing; I lucked out and got a flat tent spot.  I wanted to ask the camp host a question, but could not locate one.

reviews.author: John W.
reviews.text: Site B36 is actually on the inside of the loop across from where some campground maps show it. It is a nice site and there is room for a medium or large tent on a mostly level ground with the table and fire pit. The parking area is steeply sloped, though, and we ended up parking parallel near the road. There is a weak AT&T cell signal down right at the water’s edge of the lake. Noise from vehicles - especially logging trucks - is loud during the day. Overall it’s a good campground in a rainforest on the hill beside the lake.

reviews.author: Halie G.
reviews.text: Large area to put my tent. Will say there is a slant soo my tent wasn’t even. Overall great spot. Short walk to the bathroom

reviews.author: Dennis F.
reviews.text: Very nice campground on Lake Crescent.  Site 27 was okay for our 26 ft Airstream and Ford F150. Need to back to the passenger side to allow more room.  Nice picnic area above the site.  Near a nice bike path that was an old RR track. Good base camp to get into the west side of Olympic National Park.  Go to “Hole in the Wall” trail, and  beach #4.  Ruby Beach is very crowded.

reviews.author: Hope B.
reviews.text: The highway right there makes it so hard to sleep with the loud trucks all night. And also some of the campsites are on hills so it’s hard to sleep.

reviews.author: Jenny T.
reviews.text: The campground itself is beautiful. The trees are covered in moss, the grounds covered in ferns ...the lake is just breath taking....but the campsites are extremely close to each other.
