And WHY are there no bear lockers ...not allowed to even leave the propane tank out ..so EVERYTHING must remain in your car...which really sucks when trying to go hike all over with a car full of stuff. The location is ...beautiful but you might get car sick getting to and from there. Busy weekend ....one of the stall had no toilet paper for three of the days out of six days I was there. Weird way to wash the bathroom and leaving a puddle of water in the middle. Never saw the hosts.

reviews.author: Larissa G.
reviews.text:
ite 4 loop A

Enjoyed our base camp for doing the Olympic Discovery Trail!

Site is next to the bathrooms and has a shared bear box by the fire pit. It feels to be one of the smaller sites (although the one to the right looked smaller).
Site is ideal for a large single tent (ours was a 6P) but could comfortably do two smaller tents side by side.
Trees are spaced well for hammock camping but need to bring extra straps for more webbing (one  tree required two Eno Atlas straps to get around it).

We had two SUVs with bike racks and squeezed both into the parking spot (which looks to be relatively flat ). Since our cars took up all of the parking area, it was difficult to have access to the exit. Parking spot is like the tent space :-) better for one larger vehicle or two small ones. 

The picnic table is central which makes it hard to put a tarp over top to protect from rain. The candidate trees were just a little too far and wide around for what we brought. An awning or structure over the table would work best! 

No showers at this site, but potable water and trash are available! The Callum Transit Bus 14 (goes to Forks or Port Angeles) stops outside of the store and it’s a .25 mile walk to the camp site. It was about 4 miles with a gentle rail trail grade bike ride to the ODT! 

Had decent Verizon reception and for lighter sleepers would recommend bringing an eye mask (light from the bathroom) and ear plugs (other campers).

reviews.author: Marie B.
reviews.text: Nice walk-in spot right on the water. Only downside is there's very little room for a tent and only a small one at that. The only reasonably flat-ish spot was right next to the trail. If you've got a one or two person backpacking tent you could fit but there really isn't space for anything bigger than that.

reviews.author: Rachel  J.
reviews.text: This campground is wonderful! The bathrooms are impressive, with flush toilets! I stayed in camp site 63, which is definitely the best one in that area. It's kind of in the corner, so it has more privacy than some others. Some spots are quite in open view.

reviews.author: Cheyanne K.
reviews.text: The campground itself was good. The lake was within walking distance, and it had a dock for swimmers. I gave the campsite 4 stars because 1) the fire ring was next to the picnic table with very little room between and 2) it does not include a food locker which would have been nice to accompany the sign warning about the dangers of food and odors attracting wildlife. On the positive side, we were able to set-up our Big Agnes 6-person tent. It was a little closer to the picnic table than we prefer, but that's because we are particular about ground slope and which way the tent is facing.

reviews.author: Jackson F.
reviews.text: This site is beautiful, and has a great view of the lake - highly recommend. However, I will say it is very close to the sites on either side, and there is no cover insulating you from campers at those site. If you prefer some privacy while camping, this is not the site for you. If you are going with a group and reserved the two sites on either side for members of your group, that would be ideal.

reviews.author: Rachel H.
reviews.text:
I was very disappointed the photos/map/description for this site state it's a drive through campsite. That being said i was expecting the campground to be a one-way loop, as it was... someone had moved the cement table into the middle of the drive through preventing any easy access. we had to go wrong way through the campground to back our 16ft trailer into the spot. some spots are level and some are total slope, hit or miss what you get when you've never seen it before. this spot was not terrible but had a slope. 
I wouldn't have cared as much but being a "national park" 80% of the people visiting were rude and acted very entitled towards camping spots. I have traveled through many states and almost every national park in the central/ western states and this park by far was the rudes people i have met, let alone the park itself is not worth the drive. 
We were suppose to stay 2 nights however it turns out the trip was a bust.

reviews.author: Craig J.
reviews.text: Noise from 101 kept us both from sleep on night one, even though we had a campsite further in, the logging trucks are constant, but erratic and very loud.  Night two ear plugs (the kind provided on international flights) helped. But wouldn’t bother camping here again. Site was also barely big enough for our vehicle, tent and kitchen tent; our van is only 12 ft long.

reviews.author: Ana L.
reviews.text: Gorgeous campground. We stayed in loop B27 and the space was private and fit two tents perfectly. The bathrooms were always clean and easy to access. The lake is breathtaking. Will try to get a spot with lake view next time!

reviews.author: Ivy L.
reviews.text:
Pros: central location close to many destinations, large space for each site, clean bathrooms, close to boat launch site on Crescent Lake.
Cons: campsites close to each other with no barriers for privacy, NOISY. The highway is very close by and the noise from the cars are amplified and prevented us from sleeping well every night, even with ear plugs.

reviews.author: Cameron P.
reviews.text: Campground location is convenient for visiting Lake Crescent, Sol Duc Falls area, Mount Storm King, and Port Angeles. The walk in campsites do have access to a reserved park spot, shared bear boxes, and water spigots. However, they are kind of far from the nearest bathroom. Walk in sites have a slight grade, but not enough to make it uncomfortable. Site 81 does have a partial lake view. Not much privacy from neighboring sites but still overall a great site. You do hear the traffic from the highway during the day but overnight the roadway isn't very busy.

reviews.author: Stephanie J.
reviews.text: Quiet campground in general and our spot was mostly blocked from the road which was nice for the dogs to not be able to see walkers.  Flush potties were a close walk.  Our spot was shaded and delightful.  Cell service with AT&T was minimal.  We could walk around the campground with dogs, but most nearby trails are not open to dogs, so make sure to check that out if you're bringing dogs for hiking.

reviews.author: Patricia E L.
reviews.text: Nice site, level ground to park the camper van. Clean bathrooms.  A bit too close to the road so there was a muffled traffic sound.  Easy walk to a Beautiful clean lake.

reviews.author: Louise K.
reviews.text:
The location at the west end of Lake Crescent is fantastic, as is the proximity to the Spruce RR Grade Trail but if you are hoping to get a good night's sleep, this is not the place to camp. 
Hwy 101 is just across the narrow part of the lake and the cars and logging trucks pass through at all hours so even with ear plugs, I could hear the road noise. It was a nice place to experience, but never again.

reviews.author: Valorie M.
reviews.text:
Crescent Lake is beautiful and we enjoyed our 2 nights of camping there but the camp ground was very loud with road noise from the 101 and noisy neighbors. We ended up
moving our camp site to Sol Duc and it was much quieter.

reviews.author: Douglas C.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground and lake.  Some traffic noise.

reviews.author: Thomas G.
reviews.text: The campground is very compact and the tent sites are right on top of each other. We stayed at site #71 and our neighbors were so close it was almost as if we were at the same site. The ground was extremely compacted and it was difficult to get MSR Groundhog stakes in securely, not to mention the sloped ground at that site. Highway 101 is in view and earshot the whole time so expect a bunch of noise. Also, parking spots are numbered in correlation with the tent sites. #71 does not have a designated parking spot which was very confusing on top of the out of numerical order parking sites. Was in the Rainier/ Olympic area 11 nights and spent 7 in a tent between back country permits and front county camp sites like this. Fairholme was definitely the worst of the 7 nights.

reviews.author: Jake D.
reviews.text: Incredibly pretty water and nice clean campground. Only thing that sucks is the nighttime noise from traffic.

reviews.author: Jesse W.
reviews.text: Lovely campground. Good access to the lake, great scenery, and nice clean bathrooms. Road noise from the nearby highway was a bit annoying in the morning, but not particularly horrible. 17A was a pretty nice site with very good isolation from other campsites, but it is entirely exposed and close to the main road entrance to the campground.

reviews.author: Cheyenne R.
reviews.text: This was an absolutely beautiful campsite and the location in proximity to the lodge was nice as well in case you wanted to rent kayaks or forgot any amenities!

reviews.author: Tom S.
reviews.text: Good stop to see Crescent Lake and then head off to the coast.

reviews.author: Kat  P.
reviews.text: This location was idyllic and perfectly located for exploring Olympic National Park. It has easy access to Hurricane Ridge, Mt. Storm King, hot springs, and sits right on the beautiful lake crescent. It’s also a little more than an hour drive to Forks and the Hoh rainforest. My only negative comment is that the sound of the cars on the road echo throughout the campground and you can hear cars driving all night long regardless of whether your site is next to the water or at the back of the campground. That being said, I would stay here again but be prepared and bring ear plugs.

reviews.author: Staffan P.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground but bring earplugs for sleeping! The main road has logging trucks etc that are pretty noticeable at night. I like the moldable silicone wax earplugs for swimmers. Best i've found.

reviews.author: Cassidy P.
reviews.text:
This was a beautiful, large campsite. There were four of us, and we had plenty of space to set up 3 small tents. The view was incredible. This was possibly the most beautiful place I have ever camped. 

We did encounter a couple of issues. When we arrived, there were people in our spot. They tried to argue that the sites were first come first serve, and they wouldn’t move even after showing them my reservation. Finally, when I said I was going to get the host, they packed up and moved to another spot. We had somewhere to be and didn’t have time to tell the host about this issue. The road noise at night was also quite bad.

reviews.author: Katie J.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground, I waited to book at the 14 day window for loop C.  I had a site ready to go, and all but one site were reserved within 3 minutes, including my preferred site!  Luckily, that last site was great.   Well kept campground.  Bathrooms were very clean, but did not have soap.  Overall, can’t wait to return and convince all my friends to join us!

reviews.author: David W.
reviews.text:
Pros-a wasp nest in our site was dealt with promptly 

Generally quiet and friendly

Cons- why no soap in rest room? Very strange.

Site still had some garbage in it from previous guests

reviews.author: Patrick L.
reviews.text: My family’s favorite campground. Can’t beat a forested campground with views and access to Lake Crescent, one of the most beautiful large lakes in the country. The facilities are fine, the sites are average to AMAZING. If you are up for walk in camp sites you can’t beat camping on the lake shore. There is a beach by the boat launch that has docks for fishing and swimming, with a small store for snacks and supplies. Great for spending the day on the lake. Also near enough to Sol Duc if you want to do the hot spring or have some really great hiking.

reviews.author: Janice D.
reviews.text: Lovely campground. Very quiet, and the sites allow for much privacy. Bathrooms are clean and well stocked. And there is an outlet in the restroom for phone charging!  We will be back.

reviews.author: Rebekah K.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground, clean facilities

reviews.author: wayne g.
reviews.text: reserved spot #2, this spot does not offer a level enough spot for an RV or really a tent camp.

reviews.author: Henry P.
reviews.text: Great location, quiet, easy lake access.

reviews.author: Cynthia M.
reviews.text:
Someone stole the spot that the friends of my son had reserved. The host told them they could have another site that was supposed to be empty but someone had stolen that site too!!! The site they were finally given was extremely tiny compared to the one they had originally reserved. 

The "neighbors" at the site above us were EXTREMELY loud, talking and laughing at the tops of their voices, until well after midnight, even though quiet time starts at 10. They also ran a very loud generator for about 4 hours a day! And to top it off, they had a large campfire even though there was a burn ban on. The guy was very aggressive when I told him that there was a burn ban on. I finally had to make a complaint with a Ranger. Why are there even hosts when they can't do anything about noise or stolen reserved spots?!!

reviews.author: Barbara O.
reviews.text: Great campground. We were lucky and had nice and quiet neighbors.

reviews.author: Janette M.
reviews.text: N

reviews.author: Chris F.
reviews.text: We really enjoyed our stay at the Fairhome campground. The location is stunning! Loved swimming in the clear lake and the facilities were clean and well maintained. My only piece of feedback is that it would be great if there were showers at the park.

reviews.author: Evelyn W.
reviews.text: Nice to be so close to the gorgeous lake! We loved the campground and found that it had everything we needed. The bathrooms were great. However, we did try to look for the ranger a few times to ask about places to fish and they were not there each time we checked which was unfortunate. It was a fun place to camp though! Gets very quiet and dark at night. Lots of bugs in August so bring your mosquito repellant!

reviews.author: Myckaela H.
reviews.text: location was good but you are pretty close to your neighbors and the site is sloped. however, everyone was quiet during quiet hours so it wasn’t too bad. also sucks that there was no soap in the bathroom despite having running water and a sink.

reviews.author: Alden J.
reviews.text: Very difficult to get a two night stay: we had to await release of a campsite (at exactly 7:00 AM) to get the first night, then again at 7:00 AM the next day to get the second night.

reviews.author: Athena M.
reviews.text: The campground is pretty nice being right on the lake but it is not very tranquil as there are very audible highway sounds all night. The lake is worth having a swim in if it is warm. The walk in campsites are the closest to the lake and they have good views but there aren't enough bear bins so you are more likely going to be hauling stuff back and forth between your site and your vehicle. The bathrooms were ok but had signs about "limited toilet paper" and there was no soap. It's a nice campground but the traffic noise isn't great and I would hesitate to stay again based on that. You have been forewarned!

reviews.author: Nhi T.
reviews.text: Love it

reviews.author: Larry E.
reviews.text: Amazing Campground

reviews.author: Dane M.
reviews.text:
We stayed in site 89, which is one of the walkin sites and is along the lake. The site is absolutely beautiful, and the bear box was closer than the map made it seem. While the site was large and with stunning views, it is important to note that it isn't very flat, so consider that in anticipation of your tent arraingments.

Close to the campground is the fairhome grocery store. When we were there, it had only chips, packaged sweets, hot dogs and beer. Nice to have, but not nice if you plan on restocking food while there. 

We took a 15 minute drive for dinner at the Lake Crescent Lodge, and it was one of the better meals that I've had in a while. Expensive, but worth it. 

With the campground as our basecamp, we hikes Seven Lakes Basin (hard, but highly recommended) and finished with a dip in the Sol Duc Hot Springs Resort. We also hiked Hurricane Ridge to Hurricane Hill. Far less hard, but definitely beautiful.

I would highly recommend Fairholme Campground.

reviews.author: Maria S.
reviews.text: Great location. Not a lot of flat spots to put a ten, so make sure you have a small one.

reviews.author: Shaw W.
reviews.text: Site: 53C: very spacious site where you definitely have room to park 2 vehicles and 2-3 tents. You have some partially obstructed views of the lake through the trees. Close to one of the bathrooms which looks to have been remodeled recently and reasonably close to the Loop C bathroom as well. Only downside is the lack of privacy: the site 54 has a pretty clear view of your site and you're right above the walk-in sites below. Since the site is wide you also are pretty exposed to the loop road so not much privacy from other campers that are walking to/from their campsites.

reviews.author: Anna Mae B.
reviews.text: The campsite is clean and has an easy access to clean bathrooms.

reviews.author: Jill B.
reviews.text: B27 is a really good site. Our small pop-up camper fit fine and was easy to back in and level. B27 is one of the more private sites with beautiful ferns and trees. Site can also accommodate a large tent and is similar to B loop sites 29 and 31. Lots of small campers, small RVs, and camper vans at Fairholme, despite contradictory and confusing info on the recreation website and customer service regarding trailers and campers!

reviews.author: Karen L.
reviews.text: If you look at the campground map you can tell that the sites are really close to each other in loop B (and most of the campground in general). If you going into it knowing that then the campground and this site are great. Flat spot for tent or 2 was easy to find. Short walk to 2 different bathrooms which were always clean when I visited. The campground is on a hill but most of the sites are flat. I chose this location because it put me relatively close (within an hour) to the hurricane ridge entrance which given the limited access in summer 2023 you have to arrive to early to get in.

reviews.author: M M.
reviews.text: I booked this so we could ride the Olympic Discovery trail sections on the north side of Crescent Lake because our previous experiences had been stressful drives on 101 on the south side of the lake. I didn't realize that our campsite had a view of logging trucks on 101 and loud vehicle sounds and lights during the night. This is obviously not the campground or NPS' fault,  but my own miscalculation. The campground itself was well maintained and everything went very well... except being woken in the night by lights and horns that made it sound as if - as I could hear the person in the next site remark - "I thought a train was going to hit our tent." The lake itself is stunning. The store is a fun amenity. The Olympic Discovery Trail could use a whole lot more signage, but was fabulous once located.

reviews.author: Farah C.
reviews.text:
Amazing place- Being right in front of the lake and surrounded by so much nature makes it beautiful and magical. 
No need to drive anywhere if you’d like to hike as there’s a trail nearby. The Sol Duc Springs are a 5min drive away. The nature around the area gives this place all the stars it deserves.
Aside from the trail- I wish rangers were more present- at least do a round at night as some campers are very inconsiderate: drinking, being loud and letting kids run around with flashlights pointing them into others tents… 
This campground doesn’t have showers and the ladies restroom ran out of toilet paper - it took them TWO days to put some in- there also isn’t any soap.
This is my 5th National Park visited (I started during the pandemic) and Olympic National Park is in serious need of maintenance. The rangers are all very young and maybe they are knowledgeable- but when you have questions they provide minimal response, or say ‘idk’ or are not friendly (very different from other NP were rangers are eager to share knowledge).
In summary: The place is gorgeous - the lack of maintenance and ranger activity is extremely poor.

reviews.author: Keelan J.
reviews.text: Great location, near a swimming area and very beautiful among the trees. Despite the number of campsites and other campers, the site still felt fairly secluded due to the trees. Would recommend.

reviews.author: charles j.
reviews.text: Great location, nice campground, well maintained.  One (minor) downside is the noise of traffic across the lake, especially the big logging trucks.  It is also not close to towns/supermarkets (although there's a small store close by that sells ice, milk and other basics), so need to plan ahead supplies.  But the scenery is great and it is close to many attractions, so overall highly recommended.

reviews.author: Tanja S.
reviews.text:
- the campsites are very close to each other, there is nearly no privacy
- the way to the walk-in campsites ist very long, that wasn‘t posted on the homepage 
- the walk-in sites were really difficult to find, because there are three levels of campsites and the campsite numbers weren’t posted anywhere
- the traffic from the other site of the lake was really loud, so it wasn‘t really comfortable

reviews.author: Dustin B.
reviews.text: Great location next to Lake Crescent and the perfect tranquil space to unwind and enjoy the outdoors! Perfect for going for a day trip to Hurricane Ridge or Sol Duc Falls or even a bike ride on the discovery trail.

reviews.author: Melissa M.
reviews.text:
First off, the supposed "lakefront" spots, aren't.  We had #79 which sat above several other sites that actually were lakefront.  And we knew going in that we were in a walk-in spot however it seemed the parking spot you were assigned based on your campsite was very strangely set to be the farthest away.
The other item was that Fairholme Campground is REALLY close to HWY 101 so we essentially camped next to a VERY noisy freeway.
If you like all of that, go to Fairholme Campground.

reviews.author: Ashley M.
reviews.text: Great site but could use a bit more monitoring. People were loud into the early hours of the morning.

reviews.author: Nicole T.
reviews.text: The site by the lake was beautiful but extremely close to other campers. Our boys enjoyed playing in the lake and having the ducks wander through the campsite. While we loved being right next to the lake, the bathhouse was steeply uphill, which made an annoying walk each time haha. Otherwise, you couldn't beat the location! The provided bear box was super nice.

reviews.author: Michael C.
reviews.text: Perfect spot by the water, and the best part is the shore in front of the camp site is slightly shallow and small rocks in the water before it gets really deep, so is perfect for swimming and paddle boarding. My brother even went for a night swim .

reviews.author: Mariah shelley M.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsite. The woods are amazing the bathrooms well maintained everyone was so respectful.

reviews.author: Vanessa K.
reviews.text: This is an epic campground right next to lake crescent!

reviews.author: Ben W.
reviews.text: Good clean restrooms.

reviews.author: Brad C.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground.  Not very private especially the walkins by the lake with everyone passing through.  Worth a short visit

reviews.author: Allison K.
reviews.text:
The area for your tent is on an incline. Feels like you’re going to roll down. No bear box at this site. Fairly steep walk up to your parking spot and even more so to the bathrooms. When we were there, owls were hooting all night and the ravens started screaming early in the morning. Plus, the 101 sounds super close since the lake carries the sound very well. Loudest campground I have been in that was not due to parties. We left early because we couldn’t sleep - and I don’t think we were the only ones. 
Clean, nice restrooms, lovely view and great proximity the lake. Still wouldn’t recommend.

reviews.author: Anders E.
reviews.text: Great stay, nice beach for swimming in clear water.

reviews.author: Chris B.
reviews.text: Stunning campground in an unbeatable location.  Well maintained bathrooms.  Having the general store at the entrance is also super convenient (they have ice, firewood, drinks, snacks, and useful supplies.  About the only negative I can think of is it was very hard to hammer tent stakes into the ground because it was hard packed and mixed gravel, so bring a real hammer.

reviews.author: Greg B.
reviews.text: Lovely campground and lake. Not much else to do, but nice for a night or two.

reviews.author: Stephanie S.
reviews.text: DO NOT book this walk-in site or the sites left and right of this site, the entire site(s) is on a rather steep slope (for a camp site)! There is zero flat area for a tent, seriously uncomfortable. The photo of the lake is accurate and as pretty in person, that is the only nice thing about this site. Noisy is an understatement, it is a busy campground and top that off with hearing every car pass by on the 101 24/7 and headlights shining from across the way. Our trip was amazing and wonderful until this camp site tarnished the adventure. They work hard to keep the restrooms clean; again a busy campground and the 100s of guests aren’t always tidy and supplies do run out. The site is compact and no area for a tent to be a safe distance from the fire pit. The walk-in in portion had a few ways into the site and were simple yet steep. Everything you use must be hauled back to your car or use a community bear box with your bear containers. The Rangers are super kind and helpful.

reviews.author: Lindsay B.
reviews.text: Great spot!! Just be hesitant with any of the lower waterfront spots, it is quite a walk and hilly if you have lots of gear or can't get around well. Beautiful quiet campground.

reviews.author: Erica S.
reviews.text:
I adored this campsite! If you have a smaller car you can certainly set up your tent on the gravel behind your car, but there’s also a small spot in the woods outlined by logs that can definitely fit a tent. I set up my half dome 2+ tent there with plenty of room. 
You’re close to other campsites, but not right on top of each other. You should definitely bring your camp chair/hammock and a book down to the lake on the trail right behind the campsite. It’s the most serene campsite I’ve ever booked.

reviews.author: Elizabeth C.
reviews.text: Easy access to the lake, nice trails

reviews.author: Yun P.
reviews.text: Super quiet yet the campsites are little bit close.

reviews.author: Myles P.
reviews.text: Bathroom care could be improved but the site is beautiful reservations were easy.

reviews.author: Kathryn  L.
reviews.text: Beautiful campground, nice & quiet except for our last night (a Thursday) lots of noise from dogs, campers slamming doors, & lights. But, on our nights before it was so peaceful & the Boreal owls were being loud, it was amazing to hear them! Very central to many sites we wanted to visit including; Mora’s hole in the wall at Rialto beach, gorilla rock at Ruby beach, the tree of life at Kalaloch, Madison Falls, Marymere Falls, & Sol Duc Falls. Ancient groves was our favorite trail. If you’re a Twilight fan then you’ll love Forks & their visitor center was very resourceful.

reviews.author: Sarah B.
reviews.text: Solo traveler with a single person tent and one car, but I think you could realistically fit 3-4, two person tents or a variation and two cars. Hills are kind of steep so be mindful. Picnic table and fire pit are provided within the site but water spout and bathroom are right down the turn, both of which are in good shape. I’ve been traveling to multiple parks this season and have been mindful of bears so it was a little weird to only have one bear box for the entire campsite, however the priority is given to hiker/biker as it should be. The only other thing I would be mindful of is the mosquitoes!!

reviews.author: John K.
reviews.text: I was camping at site 83 and I would have to say it's one of the best site there right on the edge of lake. It would have been nicer if it was flatter but it was acceptable. Also, there was s food storage box right on the site as well. It's a bit of walk but for the scenery you get, I didn't mind it at all. Also, very close to the general store and boat launch so if you are planning on going into water, it's probably the best one on the campground. Overall, very happy with my stay.

reviews.author: Kenny C.
reviews.text: Great site, would definitely stay again!!

reviews.author: CECIL O.
reviews.text: Had a walk-in site down by the lake shore and other than having to climb the hill to get back up to the car, it was a pleasant experience. When I read that the sites were close together I expected a lot of noise, but it was relatively quiet until about daylight when the logging trucks started rolling down US 101, but that was not the campground's fault. A number of good hiking opportunities and most of the lakeside sites had direct access to the water. The other sites could access the lake via the boat ramp/launch area. There were squirrels and chipmunks, lots of song birds, mallards and mergansers with young'uns and an owl that visited the campsite.  The hosts were informative and very friendly. The restrooms in the area I was in were under renovation, but the portable toilets were well maintained, except for the hand sanitizer. Cell service was not good, but better than expected. Had 4G with one bar down by the lake shore and occasionally two bars.

reviews.author: Anne marie G.
reviews.text: Nice campground with clean bathrooms, great water stations. Only complaint is that the tent spot in our tent site was pavement so we could not stake our tent out. Otherwise great!

reviews.author: Claudio G.
reviews.text: Very close to neighbors

reviews.author: Hailey B.
reviews.text: I loved having beach access at the campground. Was in a central area so I was easily able to get to all the main attractions. As a person with mobility issues, it was challenging for me to get to the bathroom with my campsite being on a hill. The grounds are not flat. Get a site close to bathroom if anyone in your party struggles with hills or uses accommodations to walk.

reviews.author: Joshua D.
reviews.text: Nice campground. Good atmosphere. No soap in any of the bathrooms.

reviews.author: Annie  S.
reviews.text: It was fine

reviews.author: Bill F.
reviews.text: I've stayed at Fairholme Campground many times and I always enjoy it. The sites are spacious and not too close and the tall timber makes a great atmosphere. This year (2023) they were renovating the middle restroom, which was a little inconvenient. They had porta-potties nearby, but I just walked to the north restroom, which was renovated last year. It's just beautiful: all new tile, stalls, and sinks, etc.  I'm glad to see they're improving th campground.

reviews.author: Joelle S.
reviews.text: Lovely forested campsite about 30-45 minutes away from Storm King and Sol Duc trailheads. Not the most privacy I've had at a site, and the bathrooms were busy due to the number of sites they serve but there was a nice beach/dock area nearby to sit and watch the lake.

reviews.author: Luna Z.
reviews.text: The campground was big and pretty well maintained and it was great to have flushing toilets but lots of road noise and my site was not the most level. I would stay again but would try to find a site as far from road as possible.

reviews.author: Delia T.
reviews.text: The site is beautiful but boy the noise from the highway keeps going all night, I barely slept.

reviews.author: Donald P.
reviews.text:
Choose your site carefully depending on your camping vehicle. Many of the parking areas at the sites are not level as the campground is sloped. This may not be a problem if you are tenting and just parking a car but it is more problematic with an RV. More work should be done to level the parking spots on the sites.

There are new flush toilet restrooms but sadly no showers were built in these brand new structures.

reviews.author: Ashley  T.
reviews.text: One of our favorites while exploring Olympic! The bathrooms were good and being able to walk down to the lake was so nice. Definitely will be back!

reviews.author: matthew w.
reviews.text: Beautiful!! Walk-in sites get some road noise if you’re a light sleeper bring ear plugs but the beauty makes up for it. Other sites are much quieter and mostly well spaced from each other. Great jumping off point for the Olympics!

reviews.author: Steve R.
reviews.text: Great time and services

reviews.author: Rachael J.
reviews.text: Take what I say with a grain of salt. I am normally a dispersed camper, so very use to having lots of space and minimal/no people around me at any given time. Fairholm campground, being right on lake crescent held a lot of appeal, I am an avid kayaker and enjoy fishing. I lucked out and got a lake front camping spot. I arrived, got my parking spot and walked down to my site prior to unpacking my car.  The description of the site does say "hike in on short steep trails" I vastly underestimated what that actually meant.  It is 100% a hike down very steep mostly dirt, narrow trails that weeve in between other sites. I made it down to site 89 and it was TINY. Like only big enough for 1 small tent and it was right up next to the other sites. Close enough for me to hear entire intimate conversations of the campers on either side of me.  The campground itself is beautiful and clean/well maintained, but I will not be staying here again...everything was just too close for comfort.

reviews.author: Denise  S.
reviews.text: Quiet & beautiful setting

reviews.author: Abdalla A.
reviews.text: The lake was beautiful

reviews.author: Shambhavi B.
reviews.text: Love this campground situated right on lake crescent and it’s close proximity to the main attractions in Olympic. Stayed at site 22B, the campsites are fairly close together but you still get relative privacy. One of the flush toilets were under renovation at loop B when we visited but the others were clean and functional. Site 22B was large but sloped in a lot of places. Had to pitch our large 8x8’ tent on slight slope

reviews.author: Natrada T.
reviews.text: Wonderful and convenience to walk to 😊

reviews.author: Edaena G.
reviews.text: great pull through spot, all the other sites you have to reverse in and out. Good space for a bigger tent, but the ground is a little hard for the stakes. Other than that it's a very beautiful and green spot with a good amount of privacy. Super dark walk to the restroom.

reviews.author: Jonathan R.
reviews.text: Good

reviews.author: Linda D.
reviews.text: Beautiful site overlooking the lake.  Some highway noise from logging trucks.

reviews.author: Brianne D.
reviews.text: This is such a beautiful campground! Our first time staying at a walk-in site just feet away from the lake and we absolutely loved it. I've stayed at this campground for many years and there's not a bad site to be found! Beautiful sites, ravens, chipmunks, and very friendly ducks! There's road noise from Highway 101 that carries over the lake but by the second day I barely noticed it. The lake view was more than worth it!

reviews.author: Jerry F.
reviews.text:
The process of getting a reservation at Fairholme by using the website recreation.gov was a nightmare.  I ended up calling them by phone and after 1 1/2 hours finally got a warm body to answer.  After reserving the site with one individual she passed me to someone else to pay for it.  Another 20 minute wait.  Also, the site map of the campground is incorrect.  I pointed this out to the two “rangers” I dealt with while staying there.  They both knew the problem but had no way of fixing it.  Half of my time spent in the campground was dealing with other campers that didn’t know about the new process and couldn’t find a ranger to deal with.
The Park Service should run, not walk to try and get their money back that they paid this contractor to set up this website.  The Park Service didn’t do the American people any favors by going with the lowest bidder on this setup.
There is a good chance I will never go to this campground again which is a real shame because I’ve always had a good time in years past.
Trying to use your recreation.gov website is like going for a colonoscopy.  Not a good time.

reviews.author: Joanne L.
reviews.text: We had a great time with great friends. Campsites were designed for smaller rigs and tents.  We loved it. Restrooms were clean and fairly new. Beautiful spot.

reviews.author: Jordyn  W.
reviews.text: Campsite was great and it was really nice to be able to access trails right from the site and be a short drive to Olympic national park attractions.  The lake was beautiful, but you could hear quite a bit of amplified road noise while on or near the lake.  Fishing restrictions were confusing and unnecessary.

reviews.author: Francie R.
reviews.text: Camp too close to others.  Not a good tent site due to limited flat area only close to road. Left after one night and forfeited our reservation fee.

reviews.author: Emma H.
reviews.text: Beautiful place, clean and well kept. Marymere Falls was excellent- worth a visit. Be warned: Fairholme camp store closed earlier than the end of the camping season (at least a week out)

reviews.author: Jonathan E.
reviews.text: Campsites are spaced pretty well apart, but there's little visual privacy. It's a hilly area so my site ended up at a slight angle. Some highway noise can be heard at night. Restroom facilities were larger than Mora and Kalaloch campgrounds.

reviews.author: Paul D.
reviews.text: Convenient campground for adventures in northern part of Olympic NP. Quite noisy due to packing of campsites and nearby US-101 (with a hill that cars and trucks climb). Campsites by the lake are charming, but again packed too close together to make it very enjoyable. Some campsites also are too small for more than a couple of people.

reviews.author: Pratham M.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsite. Clean bathrooms. Right on the banks of Lake Crescent.

reviews.author: Anna B.
reviews.text: Excellent! Clean bathroom, clean campsite. Best view and beach at Lake Crescent!

reviews.author: Danielle D.
reviews.text: Camp site and fire ring was well maintained, bathrooms were nice for campground bathrooms and it's always a plus they're flushable. Only downside to the bathrooms is no hand soap.

reviews.author: Wendy V.
reviews.text: This is a great campground at Lake Crescent, with large sites and close proximity to the water. I recommend taking a swim in the impossibly blue waters of Lake Crescent. It's close to Sol Duc hot springs and Marymere falls, so there is plenty of hiking in the area.

reviews.author: erin p.
reviews.text: fairholme campground was really nice. the campsites and bathrooms were clean. and of course, crescent lake is beautiful!

reviews.author: Faith N.
reviews.text: Not much privacy or shade, but nice dish washing station, restrooms were clean, overall was okay. A bear came into our camp, most likely because the dumpsters did not lock- were not bear proof. They need to work on that. Hotsprings was close by, 5 min drive.

reviews.author: Lilly W.
reviews.text: We had reserved site 20B. Unfortunately, the parking spot was so sloped we could not level our small RV. We had to scramble to find another spot at a different campground further down the road. Very nerve-wracking in the middle of a camping trip. It would be a great thing if spots that are good for tent camping (the campsite had a lovely spot, level and smooth, behind the picnic table--perfect for a large tent), and not so great for a van or small RV could be designated as such.

reviews.author: Lynsey B.
reviews.text: N/A

reviews.author: Christiana P.
reviews.text:
I had a lovely stay at this place! It was right off the main road and you could hear traffic go by which wasn’t my favorite, but it did give me a little peace of mind because I was camping by myself this time. The lake is stunning and the water felt fantastic for early Sept ! I stayed in a spot close to the water. It had flushing toilets and potable water. The sites are pretty close together but that didn’t bother me much either since I had respectful neighbors. Theres also food storage containers provided but for the area I was in , there’s one container for every 2 camp sites, so you’ll have to share with your neighbors. This a great central point to any hikes around Lake Crescent, Olympic NP, and the coast!
I will definitely be back for a longer stay!

reviews.author: abigail k.
reviews.text: Good site that's relatively private. This campground was a little rowdy in the summer (lots of big groups), so just something to be aware of. Great lake access.

reviews.author: Ionut G.
reviews.text:
Amazing campground, with access to Lake Crescent, you can use the water access to launch a boat or a paddleboard. Close to Sol Duc, hiking in the Mt. Storm King area.
The restrooms were clean, there was water available, and the campground was well maintained.

reviews.author: Linda R.
reviews.text: We enjoyed our time here and had a lot of fun watching the salmon at Salmon Cascades on Sol Duc Rd. (a ranger suggested we do that).

reviews.author: Chisato H.
reviews.text: We were able to see the lake a little bit, which was nice. We would like to go back to get a spot that's in front of the lake next time.

reviews.author: Carolina U.
reviews.text: Absolutely loved the site and it’s proximity to Lake Crescent.

reviews.author: Natashia S.
reviews.text: Excellent stay. Gorgeous location with clean site, neighbors were respectful, flush toilets. The bathrooms don’t have soap so bring your own!

reviews.author: Chris L.
reviews.text: Fairholme is a very pleasant campground. Screening at sites and proximity to the lake is good.

reviews.author: tim g.
reviews.text: A  verynice  large site campground . Many sites are not very level which can be a challenge for many campers.

reviews.author: Bryn N.
reviews.text: Beautiful campsites, unreal sunsets and sunrises - the walk in sites are well worth the extra hassle of lugging your stuff down.

reviews.author: Felix P.
reviews.text: Very clean water , view  everything amazing!!

reviews.author: Laurie C.
reviews.text: The campground and bathrooms are clean. Water spigots are conveniently located throughout, plus some outside the toilet building. The lake is very beautiful with clear aqua water. Food lockers to discourage bears are plentiful but I did not see anyone use them. There were people who kept their food coolers out all day and overnight.  While the lake  is pretty, it is anything but serene. There is a very busy highway that runs along the lake. The traffic noise is very loud and I found it disturbing. My campsite was a walk-to that was along the lake's edge. The campsites here are quite small and so close to one another your tents are practically on top of each other. I had to wear earplugs to sleep because the traffic sound so so loud and the next tent had a snoring person in it. The lake is worth a visit, but I do not recommend camping here if you like peaceful settings with even a modicum of privacy.

reviews.author: Don X.
reviews.text: campground is clean and tidy.  Only regret is that the bathroom was in service and sealed off.

reviews.author: Jessica H.
reviews.text: Fairholme is  a lovely campground, my only complaints are that the sites are very close to each other so there isn't much privacy, and the toilets in loop A were closed for remodeling so there were porta potties that were very poorly maintained (dirty, no toilet paper). Otherwise it is a great camp ground, just a 3 min walk to the beach, lots of trails in the area. We will definitely camp here again!

reviews.author: Ivan B.
reviews.text: We stayed at campsite #76 and it was great. Lots of room for each campsite. Bathroom was clean but no soup. 2 min walk to the beach of beautiful lake. Definitely will be back.

reviews.author: Isaac M.
reviews.text: Campsites are super close together. Not the greatest spot for a tent either. Location is prime however. About an hour away from the coast and from Hurricane Ridge.

reviews.author: Lissa E.
reviews.text: Sites 90 and all the 80s are stunning waterfront walk-in sites (2 min) with incredible scenery. We had 88, which was flat and amazing. Some have angled tent pads. Noise from the highway wasn’t ideal, but the beauty made up for it. I would return in a heartbeat.

reviews.author: Adam T.
reviews.text: It was very pretty, but the sites are very close to each other.  Everyone around was very respectful and I think we all had a great time, but being a bit more spread out would have made it one of the best I’d ever stayed at!

reviews.author: Myriah H.
reviews.text: Had fun. The lake is freezing even in the middle of July.

reviews.author: Abby F.
reviews.text: This was a great campground. Positives were the location and the access to trails. Negatives were no hand soap or sanitizer in bathrooms and lack of level tent pads.

reviews.author: Guillermo M.
reviews.text: Ancient rainforest by the lake. Pefect!

reviews.author: Carolyn J.
reviews.text: Buggy and crowded.

reviews.author: Gloria H.
reviews.text: Such a wonderful stay. Tidy campsite, respectful neighbor campers, clean toilets and potable water. The crystal clear waters of Lake Crescent were amazing! Few mosquitos here and there, but not unbearable and side note: get your firewood past the campground west on the 101. It's cheaper and bigger bundles and you're supporting your locals. Look for the firewood signs. Enjoy your time!

reviews.author: Skye H.
reviews.text: Great campsite by the lake! Bathroom facilities were good (although one of them was in renovation and replaced with portable toilets while we were staying, but the second bathroom wasn't far away) and the water tasted fine. We camped while the campground was fully booked and the site still felt quiet and private. Would recommend bringing bug spray though!

reviews.author: Ryan W.
reviews.text:
This is not a great representation of the NPS. If you're just looking for a jump off point to Sol Duc entrance or even Hurricane Ridge—Elwha is closed—then go for it. We stayed in site A11. 
Pros: On a lake, some nice trees, 2 miles from Olympic entrance (NPS pass) and Olympic Discovery Trailhead (need WA pass), Most sites are shaded.
Cons:
• Connected to, but not part of the camp is a boat landing/swimming area that was packed despite warnings for swimmers itch posted, and both dog and human poop on the ground.
• The sites are on top of each other with zero privacy. Sites are not level.
• There is only one camp host (there are other host sites that just have cones in them) to serve a three-loop camp which leads to other issues including dumpsters being overloaded & trash just tossed on the ground nearby (bears?). The sites aren't being cleaned between guests, bathrooms were not cleaned during our stay. There was no soap or antiseptic. The bathrooms were filled with bugs, 1000s of bugs that swarm out of the toilet when you try to use it.
• Speaking of bathrooms...The A bathrooms are closed for repairs. That was no disclosed before we reserved the site in A loop. Probably because they have porta potties which: 1. are so full, poop is coming up OVER the toilet seat. 2. They are on a hill and urine is running out and down the road into other sites. 3. Someone notched peep holes over the end units looking at the urinal. WTF.
• Finally, there is a camp store. The store is currently cash only. Not a big deal in itself, but there are signs listing prices on things like food and ice and stickers, etc that are all wrong. So when you go to the register you get charged way more than expected. When you say, "Hey, why am I being charged so much? The sign says 'X'" the response is a shrug and a,"Whattya gonna do." Literally, pointing out that you're 20 miles away from other options, so pay the $9 for wood.

reviews.author: esperanza  R.
reviews.text: Site 27 looks isolated, but there is just one log between 27 and site 3. It didn't look like that in the map.

reviews.author: Kevin A.
reviews.text: Beautiful setting but there was garbage in our site, the bathrooms were portables, there was no soap. The site was not level.

reviews.author: RAJU A.
reviews.text: Great location. Close to Olympic national park. It’s on nice crescent lake. Beautiful campground between rain forest.

reviews.author: Travis C.
reviews.text: We had a reservation for 35B which supposedly fits a 20 foot trailer. We got there and there was no way a trailer would fit in there since it was sloped, small, and a log went through the middle of the camp spot. This camping site should be labeled tent only. We ended up getting a spot down the road at Shadow Mtn, it was a relief they had vacancy since it was 6pm on a Saturday Night. I talked to the ranger letting him know about the situation and requested a refund, which was approved. I was thankful they provided a refund, but wished that log didn't go through the middle of the camping spot so I could have stayed there for the whole week.

reviews.author: Nicolai G.
reviews.text: Nice campground.

reviews.author: Rebecca P.
reviews.text: Being on the water absolutely made the steep hike to and from the bathroom worth it. We have a wagon which made trips to and from the car much easier and I couldn’t imagine camping here without it.

reviews.author: Félix M.
reviews.text: Really nice

reviews.author: Elma H.
reviews.text: Overall a great campsite right on the edge of the lake. Was able to fit two 4-person tents with plenty of space to walk around. Only had neighbors on the right side (site 89). There is a site right above this one that has a clear view down. The walk to the bathrooms and car is a little steep. There was no food storage box for this site.

reviews.author: Genevieve A.
reviews.text: Amazing campground setting, lots of privacy, very easily oriented for shared bathrooms, trash disposal, etc.

reviews.author: Linda C.
reviews.text: I wish we had known that the bathroom facilities closest to our tent site were under renovation. Perhaps I just missed it in the details of the campground.  We would have looked for something else that may have opened up. It made cooking, cleaning, and personal care difficult. The site also was not very level for a tent. We are grateful, however, for National Parks campgrounds and would have still booked it if another else was available.

reviews.author: Christopher l.
reviews.text:
Overall a pretty good camping spot. Only two complaints about this site:
I had some issues with mosquitos at night.
There is a road behind this camping spot that you can hear cars drive by. It's infrequent so not much of a problem but there was one really loud car at night that woke me up.

reviews.author: Morgan R.
reviews.text: The campground is beautiful and well maintained. Very close to the water so you can walk out to the shore on there is a small dock. Bathrooms are well kept. We had a great experience!

reviews.author: Ryan S.
reviews.text: Nestled in the woods and a 30 second walk to Lake Crescent. We also lucked out with our campsite, it was huge and in a great location.

reviews.author: Margot F.
reviews.text: This might not *technically* be rainforest but it seems like the lines are fairly blurred on the penninsula for what is and isn't rainforest because we visited some rainforests and this really seemed like one to me. Altitude is higher though than Hoh, Sol Duc, Kalaloch, and Mora though so it was very cold at night. Our site was pretty far from the bathroom and walking through the forested path through the campground to get there in the middle of the night felt kind of spooky. Lots of ravens and interesting mosses and fungi. Fire will be a challenge due to the wetness. Like all the other campgrounds we stayed at in Olympic, soap, paper towels, firewood, and staff all hard to find. Still very lovely and I'm glad to have had the opportunity to stay here.

reviews.author: Albert  M.
reviews.text: As always, camping there provides an ideal setting.  It was unfortunate that multiple campers who did not know the site had changed to reservations only and the campground was listed as full and they were turned away.  However during our stay multiple campsites that were reserved for the two days had no one show up. I know this is an issue at all national park campgrounds so some type of penalty needs to be applied since the few dollars charged and not used is not a deterrent in preventing people from just not showing up and failing to cancel their reservation.  A change to a penalty of “all” reservations being cancelled for the following two months at ALL national park campgrounds would seem to provide more incentive to cancel in advance.  It would of course require the camp host to have a way to log onto a central database for this to occur.

reviews.author: Aaron C.
reviews.text: Campgrounds very nice and the sites maintained well.  Only disappointment was the old outdoor auditorium where they used to give ranger presentations is totally abandoned and overgrown.

reviews.author: Eric D.
reviews.text: Lake Crescent is magnificent. The campground itself leaves much to be desired. Neighboring sites are far too close together and, as an outdoor enthusiast, I find that overwhelming human presence detracts from the experience. I really wish our National Parks system would take this into consideration when designing the layout of campgrounds. I understand the idea is to meet demand, but opportunities to stay and enjoy nature the way I prefer are so limited. If walk in sites could actually lead a decent way out from other campers, so one wouldn't feel self conscious about holding a normal conversation, around a fire, while waiting for the stars to come out, that would be an amazing thing. Also having people's enthusiastic children scream and run through your site all evening detracts from the feeling I am after.

reviews.author: Jerry R.
reviews.text:
Beautiful area.  Ecosystem was very different than anything I'd ever seen.  Campground was clean and well maintained.
Negatives:
- no Verizon cell coverage
- site generally not very level
- logging trucks were very noisy early in the morning, primarily from the compression brakes they're not supposed to be using!

reviews.author: Abigail P.
reviews.text:
Great campground! Facilities were clean. One of the bathrooms was closed when I was there but didn't cause a problem for me. The lake is beautiful!! Many great hikes in the area (storm king for one!) that are worth the trek.

Removed one star from the campground/site because the sites are rather close together. Not necessarily a problem unless you have loud or rambunctious neighbors.

reviews.author: Lisa N.
reviews.text: Fairholme campground was beautiful - I felt like I was in a lush green rainforest.  Some of the campsites were situated right on Lake Crescent.

reviews.author: Lorraine O.
reviews.text: I am very pleased and impressed with Fairholme Campground. Bathrooms were clean, easy access to trash containers, sites are well marked, bulletin board has good information such as weather, camp sites reserved, map layout of campsites and restrooms; paved pathway connected to other loops and to restrooms, variety of campsites to accommodate RVs, small camper vans, cars, a big plus for tenters only down at the beach, good parking on sites, easy access to beach, life jackets at beach, a couple of docks. I am anxious to be back!

reviews.author: Alex S.
reviews.text: Must pack handsoap. No formal pad sites. Sites are very close together. Campground Loop A is portapotties but B has proper restrooms. No showers.

reviews.author: Rhea H.
reviews.text: Beautiful area,  campground clean and quiet, nice trails to hike and pet friendly for our golden retriever. No complaints except a rainy night but we were tucked in after evening fire.

reviews.author: Christopher E.
reviews.text: Fairholme Campground was a great and family friendly campground on Lake Crescent. It's a great place to camp if you're trying to see the sites around the lake and there's even a boat ramp if you want to bring your own Canoe/Kayak. There are two groups of bathrooms, one was under renovations during our stay but still had access to water outside.

reviews.author: Sofia B.
reviews.text: The campground is beautiful, we camped at spot 72 and it had a great view. The only downside of this campground is the proximity to the main road that goes around the lake. The logging trucks are super loud, which I wasn’t expecting, and impacted the magic of camping in such a beautiful location, which is a shame. Other than that it was a great place to camp at, I would love to go back when it’s warmer and I can take the paddle board out on the lake!

reviews.author: Peter L.
reviews.text: Beautiful Campsite.  The logging trucks on the highway at all hours is a deal breaker.

reviews.author: Samuel L.
reviews.text: Campground is beautiful but nevertheless a low score from us this time. I’ll be the Karen for this review. Our site A3 had no fire pit, just some makeshift fire hole on the ground next to the table. Good thing i had my small grill we managed to cook something.  Neighboring sites were way too close and the people on one of the sites right next to us were just yelling at each all morning. Add all the people on the walk path and cars going up and down the road bordering our site. The loop A bathroom was closed under construction replaced by porta potties that were never cleaned through our stay. We used loop B bathroom which was mostly clean and heated. Avoid site A3 if you need a fire pit with grate and some privacy. Most campsites were very small and some didn’t even have a picnic table. The grounds and lake are gorgeous though. Good if you have a small rv or camper van. Maybe we’ll try another site later

reviews.author: Paul F.
reviews.text: What a beautiful campground! Fairholme is situated in a lush, green forest on the shores of Lake Crescent, which provide a stunning landscape to camp in. The amenities are great and the campsites are well-spaced and well-sized. Only downside for me was the nearby US101: I was awoken frequently throughout the night by cars driving by Lake Crescent.

reviews.author: Mannika K.
reviews.text: Someone was in my tent site when I arrived even though we reserved the site

reviews.author: Lisa K.
reviews.text: Easy access right off 101 at the tip of Crescent Lake. Small campsites with some located on an incline. Arrived while one of the restrooms was under construction for maintenance, but luckily did not feel crowded in the remaining restrooms. Potable water was clean and fresh tasting. Lack of shower facilities was less of an inconvenience than expected. The noise of traffic through the day and night was much louder than expected.

reviews.author: Phillip A.
reviews.text: Great campsite with awesome views and good facilities.

reviews.author: Leighton H.
reviews.text: Location and access to the Olympic Peninsula was great. Where I deducted stars is for lack of water near the sites, only water in the camp is located at the bathrooms. Any sites at the top of the campground back up directly to a road, this was no clear when book and as I have a 2 year old I though being further from the late would be safer and didn't realize the road was right next to my site.

reviews.author: Jacqueline  M.
reviews.text:
This is a lovey campground in a treed forested area on a lake. Nice to walk around with dogs. It is set into a hill and some of the spots are quite small.
I got lucky and my 18’ trailer fit fine, was pretty level.
Bathrooms were very clean
